1	---
2	title: "Audio fades"
3	description: Fade a clip's sound in and out from the inspector or the handles on the clip, and choose the shape of each fade.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A fade brings a clip's sound up from silence at its start or down to silence at its end, so it doesn't begin or stop abruptly. Fades change the sound only.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Fades', 'The fade handles on a clip']}
12	  tools="set_audio"
13	/>
14	
15	## Set a fade length
16	
17	Open the **Fades** section on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/) and set the lengths.
18	
19	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
20	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
21	| **Fade in** | How long the sound takes to rise from silence at the clip's start. | 0 | 0 to 10 s |
22	| **Fade out** | How long the sound takes to fall to silence at the clip's end. | 0 | 0 to 10 s |
23	
24	The field's chevron offers 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 s. A length you type here is kept exactly as typed, not rounded to whole frames.
25	
26	The section's summary shows both lengths, such as "0.50 · 1.00 s", or "none". **Reset** clears both lengths and leaves the shapes as they are.
27	
28	With an [action selected](/audio/animate-sound/), these two rows write the action's end state.
29	
30	## Drag a fade handle
31	
32	Every clip with sound has a small square handle at each top corner of its audio part. Drag the left handle inward to set the fade in, or the right handle inward to set the fade out. The handle then sits at the end of the fade.
33	
34	The handles and the inspector rows change the same two settings, with these differences:
35	
36	- A handle's length snaps to whole frames.
37	- A handle can go past 10 s, up to the length of the clip. The 10 s limit is the inspector's.
38	- A handle changes that one clip, not the whole selection, and it doesn't select the clip.
39	- A handle changes the clip's own fade, even with an action selected.
40	
41	Each drag is one undo step, "Set Fade". Handles don't snap to clip edges, markers or the playhead, because a fade is a length, not a position.
42	
43	Handles don't respond on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). They aren't drawn when the clip's audio part is under 10 pt tall.
44	
45	## Choose a fade shape
46	
47	**In shape** and **Out shape** set how the level moves across each fade. The default for both is **Linear**.
48	
49	| Shape | On a fade in | On a fade out | Level halfway |
50	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
51	| **Linear** | A straight ramp, the same amount every moment. | The same in reverse. | 50 % |
52	| **S-Curve** | Starts and ends gently, moving fastest in the middle. | The same. | 50 % |
53	| **+3 dB** | Rises quickly, then levels off. Good for a fade in that should be heard straight away. | Holds up, then falls quickly at the end. | 71 %, 3 dB under full |
54	| **−3 dB** | Starts slowly and gathers speed. | Falls quickly, then trails away. Good for a fade out that should feel long. | 29 %, about 11 dB under full |
55	
56	The shapes always belong to the clip itself. With an action selected they're marked ⊘ and still change the clip's own setting, and an action can't [animate](/audio/animate-sound/#what-cant-be-animated) them.
57	
58	A crossfade between two clips has its own shape, with the same four choices. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/).
59	
60	## When a clip moves or is trimmed
61	
62	A fade is measured from the clip's own edges:
63	
64	- **Move** a clip and the fade travels with it.
65	- **Trim** a clip and the fade stays at the edge, the same length.
66	- **Split** a clip and both halves keep both fade lengths, so a fade in also starts the second half and a fade out also ends the first.
67	
68	Where a fade in and a fade out overlap, the two multiply. That gives a dip in the middle rather than a jump. A length you type can be longer than the clip, and that fade is then cut off at the clip's other edge, so the sound never reaches full level.
69	
70	## Good to know
71	
72	- On a [nest clip](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-on-a-nest), fades scale everything inside the nest.
73	- The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) shows a clip's fades, so you can see them against the level.
74	
75	## With an agent
76	
77	`set_audio` sets a fade's length and shape on one or more clips, with `fade_in`, `fade_out`, `fade_in_shape` and `fade_out_shape`. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#fades-and-fade-shapes). A crossfade is set with `set_transition_style` instead. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/).
78	
79	## Related
80	
81	- [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/)
82	- [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/)
83	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)

1	---
2	title: "Crossfades"
3	description: "Fade one clip's sound into the next across a transition, choose the shape of the fade, and crossfade clips that have no picture."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	When two clips on a track overlap with a transition, the transition can fade the outgoing sound out and the incoming sound in, so the cut isn't heard as a jump.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition section"
13	  tools="set_transition_style"
14	/>
15	
16	## Crossfade audio
17	
18	A new transition already crossfades its sound, at the **+3 dB** shape, so most of the time there's nothing to do. Open the section to turn the crossfade off, or to change its shape.
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Select the later of the two overlapping clips, on its own. The **Transition** section only appears for a single clip that overlaps the clip before it.
23	
24	2. In the Clip tab, choose the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Transition**.
25	
26	3. Tick or untick **Crossfade Audio**.
27	
28	</Steps>
29	
30	| **Crossfade Audio** | What you hear across the overlap |
31	| --- | --- |
32	| On | The outgoing sound fades out and the incoming sound fades in. If only one of the two clips has sound, that clip still fades. |
33	| Off | Both clips play at their own level for the whole overlap, mixed together. |
34	
35	The fade follows the transition's **Curve**, so an eased transition eases its sound too. A new transition is **Ease In Out**. **Curve** and **Crossfade Audio** are separate settings, and changing one leaves the other alone.
36	
37	To change the overlap's length, use the **Duration** row. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
38	
39	## Choose a crossfade shape
40	
41	**Crossfade Shape** sets the curve of the fade. It's available while **Crossfade Audio** is on, and the default is **+3 dB**. The incoming clip follows the shape, and the outgoing clip follows it in reverse.
42	
43	| **Crossfade Shape** | What it does | Each clip's level halfway through the fade |
44	| --- | --- | --- |
45	| **Linear** | A straight-line pair. It dips 3 dB in the middle of two unrelated takes, but suits two parts of the same sound. | About −6 dB |
46	| **S-Curve** | A fade that does most of its changing in the middle of the overlap and moves slowly at both ends. | About −6 dB |
47	| **+3 dB** | Constant power, which holds the level steady across two unrelated takes. | About −3 dB |
48	| **−3 dB** | A slow start. The incoming sound rises late and the outgoing sound falls early, so the middle of the overlap is the quietest of the four. | About −11 dB |
49	
50	## Audio-only transitions
51	
52	Two overlapping clips with no picture get the same **Transition** section, on the same sub-tab. Only their sound changes. **Crossfade Audio**, **Crossfade Shape** and **Curve** control the fade, **Duration** sets its length, and **Kind** has no visible effect.
53	
54	Whenever an edit makes a clip overlap the one before it, Frame Job adds a transition, for audio clips as for any other. So overlapping two music clips crossfades them straight away. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) for the other ways to make one.
55	
56	## Crossfade after Detach Audio
57	
58	[Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) moves a clip's sound to its own clip on the track below and switches it off on the picture clip, so **Crossfade Audio** on the transition between two picture clips no longer fades that sound. The fade belongs to the detached audio clips instead.
59	
60	Detach both clips of an overlap and their audio clips overlap on that track, which gives them a transition of their own that crossfades them. Audio clips that don't overlap yet get one as soon as you overlap them. Select the later audio clip to change it.
61	
62	## Good to know
63	
64	- The crossfade multiplies whatever else is happening to the sound. Mute, solo, ducking, volume and a clip's own fades still apply on top.
65	- With **Kind** set to **None**, an overlap has no transition of its own. It plays as a linear cross dissolve with no sound crossfade, and the section shows **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** off. Changing either of them gives the overlap a transition with exactly the values shown.
66	- Choosing another style from **Clip ▸ Transition** on a clip that already has a transition keeps its curve and its crossfade.
67	- A transition on a nest clip fades all the sound inside the nest. A crossfade between clips inside the nest still happens too, and you hear both.
68	- Each clip's [limiter](/audio/limiter/) holds that clip alone, so two limited clips can add up past the ceiling during an overlap. An export's master limiter catches this, but the preview has none, so it can sound louder while you edit. A [track compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) is also approximate in the preview where clips overlap.
69	
70	## With an agent
71	
72	`set_transition_style` sets the crossfade with `audio` (true or false) and its shape with `audio_shape`: `plus_3db`, `linear`, `s_curve` or `minus_3db`. A key you leave out keeps what's there. See [Tools: transitions](/mcp/tools-transitions/#set_transition_style).
73	
74	## Related

76	- [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/)
77	- [Audio fades](/audio/fades/)
78	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
79	- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)

1	---
2	title: "Pan and Mix to mono"
3	description: "Move a stereo clip's balance left or right, fold its channels into one, and place a sound anywhere between the speakers."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The **Mix** section places a clip's sound between the speakers. **Pan** moves a stereo clip's balance, and **Mix to mono** folds its channels into one.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Mix"
12	  tools="set_audio"
13	/>
14	
15	The section's header summarises it: "centre", "mono", or the pan position. **Detach Audio** and **Attach Audio** are on the same section, and have [their own page](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
16	
17	## Pan a clip
18	
19	Drag **Pan**, type a number from −100 to 100, or use a quick pick: −100, −50, 0, 50 or 100. Negative numbers go left, positive numbers go right, and the default is 0.
20	
21	**Position**, under it, reads the result in words: "centre", "left 30" or "right 100". It's a readout, so there's nothing to set there.
22	
23	On a stereo clip, **Pan** is a balance control. It doesn't move the left channel's sound across to the right:
24	
25	- At the centre, nothing changes.
26	- Moving it one way turns that side up and the other side down, keeping the total power steady.
27	- At −100 or 100, the side it went to is about 3 dB louder than at the centre, and the other side is silent.
28	
29	Pan has no effect on a mono file. See [Good to know](#good-to-know).
30	
31	## Mix to mono
32	
33	**Mix to mono** averages all of the clip's channels into one and sends that to every channel. It's off by default.
34	
35	On a one-channel file it does nothing, because there's nothing to fold.
36	
37	If only one channel of a stereo file has anything on it, use [Channels](/audio/channels/) instead. Averaging a voice with a silent channel halves its level.
38	
39	## Place a stereo clip's sound anywhere
40	
41	To hear a true pan, tick **Mix to mono** as well as setting **Pan**. The fold happens before the pan, so both channels carry the same sound, and **Pan** places that one sound anywhere from left to right.
42	
43	## Animate them
44	
45	With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, both controls write what the action changes to. **Pan** glides there across the action. **Mix to mono** is a switch, so it changes at the action's end, and its row says "at end". See [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
46	
47	## Reset the section
48	
49	**Reset** on the section's header sets the pan back to centre and turns mono off. It appears while the section differs from its default and no action is selected. See [Reset a section](/getting-started/inspector-fields/#reset-a-section).
50	
51	## Good to know
52	
53	- Pan has no effect on a mono file, with or without **Mix to mono**, because the file still has only one channel when Pan acts on it. A [track's pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) can't move it either.
54	- On a nest clip, **Pan** has no effect. Set it on the clips inside.
55	- **Mix to mono** on a nest clip does work: it folds everything inside the nest, and that flattens any panning on the clips and tracks in it.
56	- The Volume section's **Loudness** readout counts Pan and Mix to mono on a stereo clip, and so does [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode.
57	- In the clip's chain of sound processing, this section comes after the [compressor](/audio/compressor/) and before the [limiter](/audio/limiter/).
58	
59	## With an agent
60	
61	`set_audio` sets these with `pan`, from −1 for hard left to 1 for hard right (the inspector's −100 to 100), and `mono`, true or false. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#mono-keep-pitch-pan-and-channels).
62	
63	## Related
64	
65	- [Channels](/audio/channels/)
66	- [Track volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/)
67	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)

1	---
2	title: "Channels"
3	description: "Choose which channels of a stereo file play, to fix a microphone recorded on one side or swap left and right."
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	**Channels** chooses which channels of a stereo file a clip plays. It's the fix for a microphone recorded onto one side of a stereo file, which otherwise plays from one speaker only.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Channels"
12	  tools="set_audio"
13	/>
14	
15	## Choose channels
16	
17	Open the **Channels** section and pick from **Play**. With several clips selected, the choice goes to all of them.
18	
19	| **Play** | What you hear |
20	| --- | --- |
21	| **Both** | The file as it is. This is the default. |
22	| **Left Only** | The left channel, from both speakers. |
23	| **Right Only** | The right channel, from both speakers. |
24	| **Swap Left and Right** | The two channels exchanged. |
25	
26	For a microphone on one channel, choose **Left Only** or **Right Only**. The voice then plays from both speakers at its own level. [Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/#mix-to-mono) would also put it in both speakers, but averaging it with the silent channel halves its level.
27	
28	The header of the section shows the current choice. **Reset** there puts it back to **Both**.
29	
30	## Good to know
31	
32	- A mono file has only one channel, so the choice has no effect on it.
33	- On a nest clip the choice has no effect. Set it on the clips inside.
34	- The Volume section's **Loudness** readout counts the choice, and so does [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode. Normalize in Peak mode reads the file's waveform and doesn't.
35	- The choice comes after [voice isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) and any [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/), and before the [EQ](/audio/eq/) and [Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/#mix-to-mono). So on a stereo file with a voice effect, it picks from the sound after the effect.
36	- With an [action](/motion/edit-an-action/) selected, the choice is what the action changes to. It switches at the action's end with no glide, and its row says "at end".
37	
38	## With an agent
39	
40	`set_audio` sets this with `channels`: `both`, `left`, `right` or `swapped`. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#mono-keep-pitch-pan-and-channels).
41

1	---
2	title: "Normalize"
3	description: "Set each selected clip's volume from a measurement of the clip, to a loudness target that matches clips or to a peak level."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	Normalize sets each selected clip's volume from a measurement of the clip, so you don't have to set levels by ear. In its default Loudness mode, every clip lands at the same loudness, which is how you make clips match.
11	
12	<AtAGlance
13	  menu="Clip ▸ Normalize"
14	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Volume"
15	  tools="normalize_clip"
16	/>
17	
18	<Shot
19	  name="09-clip-sound.inspector"
20	  alt="The Sound sub-tab's Volume section for an audio clip: Volume at 100%, a Gain of +0.0 dB, Loudness and At volume both reading −21.8 LUFS and −20.8 dBTP, a Mute checkbox, a Normalize row set to Loudness at −16.0 LUFS, and the Normalize and Enhance Voice buttons."
21	/>
22	
23	## Normalize a clip
24	
25	<Steps>
26	
27	1. Select one or more clips.
28	
29	2. On the **Sound** sub-tab, open the **Volume** section and check the **Normalize** row: the mode, and in Loudness mode the target.
30	
31	3. Press **Normalize**, or choose **Clip ▸ Normalize**. The two do the same thing and follow that row. There's no keyboard shortcut.
32	
33	</Steps>
34	
35	However many clips are selected, it's one undo step, named "Normalize". That step also takes back any limiter it turned on.
36	
37	It replaces the clip's volume rather than adding to it, so pressing it a second time changes nothing, and that second press beeps. **Mute** is left as it is.
38	
39	## Choose a mode
40	
41	The first control in the **Normalize** row picks what Normalize aims at.
42	
43	| Mode | What it aims at | Matches clips? |
44	| --- | --- | --- |
45	| **Peak** | Each clip's loudest moment reaches −1 dBFS. | No |
46	| **Loudness** | Each clip's overall loudness reaches the target, −16 LUFS unless you choose another. This is the default. | Yes |
47	
48	The mode and the target belong to the app, not the project. They're kept between launches, and changing them isn't an undo step.
49	
50	## Set the loudness target
51	
52	The field beside the mode sets the level in LUFS, from −50 to −5. The default is −16, and it's only live in Loudness mode. The quick picks are:
53	
54	| Target | What it's for |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| −14 LUFS | YouTube's playback reference |
57	| −16 LUFS | The default |
58	| −23 LUFS | The EBU R 128 broadcast level |
59	
60	[Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) aims at the same target, and the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) draws it as a line.
61	
62	## Loudness mode
63	
64	Loudness mode sets each clip's volume so its integrated loudness reaches the target. That's the BS.1770 measure of the clip as a whole, as the export plays it, in LUFS, the unit of loudness. The volume can go down as well as up.
65	
66	- **It watches the peaks.** A clip whose true peak would pass −1 dBTP at that volume gets its [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) turned on at −1 dBTP in the same step, and the volume is the one that reaches the target through the limiter.
67	- **It keeps a limiter you set.** A clip that already has one keeps it, with its ceiling lowered to −1 dBTP if it was higher.
68	- **It stops at 3200 %.** A clip that would need more stops there and lands quieter than the target.
69	
70	## Peak mode
71	
72	Peak mode sets each clip's volume so its loudest moment reaches −1 dBFS. The level is fixed, and it happens at once, with no sheet. It reads the file's waveform, so the clip's EQ, clean-up and other processing don't count.
73	
74	Each clip gets its own gain, so levels don't match across a selection: a sparse voice still sounds quieter than a dense one. A clip whose peak is quieter than about −31 dBFS can't reach −1 dBFS. It's turned up to 3200 % and stops there.
75	
76	## What Normalize measures
77	
78	Normalize measures the clip, not the mix. It reads the clip's waveform (Peak) or loudness analysis (Loudness) over the part of the file that actually plays, so a trimmed clip is measured on what's left.
79	
80	The clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo don't affect the reading, and neither do its track's volume and pan. In Loudness mode, the clip's own **Channels**, **Mix to mono** and **Pan** do count on a stereo clip. A mono clip is measured on both channels, as the export plays it, which reads 3 dB louder than the file on its own.
81	
82	## Measure through a clip's processing
83	
84	Cleaning up a clip changes how loud it measures, so the analysis alone would miss the target. In Loudness mode, a clip with any of these is rendered through them as the export plays it, and its volume is set from what comes out:
85	
86	- An active [EQ](/audio/eq/)
87	- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)
88	- [Voice isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
89	- [Noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
90	- A [gate](/audio/gate/)
91	- The [leveller](/audio/leveller/)
92	- A [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/)
93	- A [compressor](/audio/compressor/)
94	- A [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/)
95	
96	With the limiter on as well, Normalize renders again at the volume it chose, and adjusts until the result is within 0.1 LU of the target, at most three times. A clip measured this way keeps its volume when the new one is within 0.05 dB of it and its limiter hasn't changed, so a second press still changes nothing.
97	
98	This takes a moment per clip, seconds on a long one, and the first press waits for the clip's voice isolation or voice effect to render. A clip with none of this processing is measured from the analysis at once.
99	
100	Until Normalize or Enhance Voice has measured such a clip, the **At volume** readout shows "≈" in front of its figures, because they're from before the processing. See [Clip volume](/audio/volume/).
101	
102	## The Measuring Sound sheet
103	
104	While clips are rendered through their processing, a **Measuring Sound** sheet shows a progress bar and "Clip 1 of 2…", counting only the clips that need a render. Editing commands are off until it closes. [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) use the same sheet.
105	
106	Nothing changes until every clip is measured, and **Cancel** leaves everything as it is. If the project changes while it measures, nothing changes, Frame Job beeps, and a sentence at the foot of the inspector says to choose the command again.
107	
108	## Clips Normalize skips
109	
110	Normalize leaves out the clips below and still does the rest. The button and the menu item are greyed out when no selected clip plays sound, or when only nests are selected. A press that changes nothing beeps, and neither the button nor the menu says which clips were skipped or why.
111	
112	| Skipped | Why | Mode |
113	| --- | --- | --- |
114	| Nests | Their level lives in the clips inside them. Open the nest and normalize those, or set the nest clip's volume by hand. | Both |
115	| Shapes, titles, stills and movies with no sound | There's no sound to measure. A clip with its sound switched off counts too. | Both |
116	| A clip not analysed yet | Its waveform or loudness is still being worked out, which often happens straight after an import. The **Loudness** readout says "measuring…" meanwhile. | Both |
117	| A silent clip | It's silent over the part that plays. In Loudness mode that means quieter than −70 LUFS throughout. | Both |
118	| A very short clip | It plays for under 0.4 s, too short for a loudness measurement. | Loudness |
119	| A clip whose reversed copy is still being made | It can't be rendered yet. | Loudness, through processing |
120	| A clip whose processing can't be rendered | There's nothing to measure. | Loudness, through processing |
121	| A clip that's too quiet after its processing | It's quieter than −70 LUFS after it. | Loudness, through processing |
122	
123	## Good to know
124	
125	- Normalize writes the clip's base level, even with the playhead inside an action. With an action selected, the button carries a small boxed "clip" tag to show this. If an action animates the volume, its values still win for as long as it runs.
126	- It can go past the slider's 400 %, up to the 3200 % ceiling, about +30 dB.
127	- The result for a limited clip with no other processing is worked out from the analysis, not rendered, so the export can land slightly off it.
128	- A clip played at a speed other than ×1, or ramped, reads to within about 0.5 LU of what plays. A file with more than two channels has its loudness measured from a two-channel mix of it.
129	
130	## With an agent
131	
132	`normalize_clip` names its own mode and doesn't read the **Normalize** row. In Peak mode it can aim anywhere from −60 to 0 dBFS, and it reports what each clip measured, where it landed, and each skipped clip with its reason. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/#normalize_clip).
133	
134	## Related
135

137	- [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/)
138	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
139	- [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)

1	---
2	title: "Enhance Voice"
3	description: "Measure a voice recording and set up its cleaning, dynamics and volume in one step, with ordinary settings you can see and change."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Enhance Voice sets a clip up for speech in one step. It measures the voice and the pauses, chooses the clean-up and dynamics the recording needs, and sets the volume that reaches your loudness target.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Enhance Voice"
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Volume"
14	  tools="enhance_voice"
15	  needs="Nothing. Speech detection and voice isolation run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
16	/>
17	
18	## Enhance a voice
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Select one or more clips with speech in them.
23	
24	2. Check the target in the **Normalize** row of the **Volume** section. It's −16 LUFS unless you've [chosen another](/audio/normalize/#set-the-loudness-target).
25	
26	3. Press **Enhance Voice**, or choose **Clip ▸ Enhance Voice**.
27	
28	4. Wait for the [Measuring Sound sheet](/audio/normalize/#the-measuring-sound-sheet) to finish.
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	However many clips are selected, it's one undo step, named "Enhance Voice". **Cancel** in the sheet changes nothing. If the project changes while it measures, nothing changes either, and a sentence at the foot of the inspector says to choose the command again.
33	
34	Everything it writes is an ordinary setting, so you can see and change each one in its own section. Pressing it again changes nothing and beeps, and so does [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) at the same target afterwards.
35	
36	To run it on a recording as soon as the recording lands, see [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).
37	
38	## What it measures
39	
40	It reads the clip before any of the settings it's about to write: its loudness and true peak, and, every 10 ms of the part that plays, whether the clip is speaking or pausing. It needs at least a second of speech, and half a second of pause to measure the noise between words.
41	
42	## What it sets
43	
44	Each of these is a separate decision, made from the clip's own measurements.
45	
46	### Rumble cut
47	
48	It always sets the [EQ](/audio/eq/)'s **Rumble Cut**, a high-pass at 80 Hz, 24 dB/oct, to take out low rumble, and keeps the EQ's other parts.
49	
50	### Noisy pauses
51	
52	The pauses count as noisy when their median loudness is less than 45 dB under the clip's loudness.
53	
54	| The pauses are | What it does |
55	| --- | --- |
56	| Noisy | Turns on [voice isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) at 80 % with noise reduction off, and fits a [gate](/audio/gate/) to the pauses. |
57	| Noisy, on a clip with a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame | Turns on [noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) at 50 % with voice isolation off, because isolation can't serve that clip, and fits the gate. |
58	| Quiet | Turns voice isolation, noise reduction and the gate off. |
59	| Under half a second long in total | Leaves all three as they are, because there's nothing to measure. |
60	
61	The gate opens 10 dB above the pauses' median true peak, held between −40 and −6 dB relative to the clip's loudness.
62	
63	### Leveller
64	
65	It turns on the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) at its defaults when the speech's loudness varies a lot from moment to moment, meaning its short-term loudness range is over 6 LU. The range is measured over 3-second stretches of the speech alone. At or under 6 LU the leveller is turned off, and with under 3 seconds of speech it's left as it is.
66	
67	### De-esser
68	
69	It turns on the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) at its defaults when at least 5 % of the speech has a hot "s" band: 6 kHz and up, within 10 dB of the clip's loudness. Otherwise it's turned off.
70	
71	### Compressor, limiter and final volume
72	
73	Every clip it enhances gets all three, whatever else it measured.
74	
75	- A [compressor](/audio/compressor/) at 3:1, its threshold at the speech's median true peak, with makeup that gives back the loudness it takes.
76	- The [limiter](/audio/limiter/). The clip keeps its own, with the ceiling at most −1 dBTP, or gets the default.
77	- The volume that takes the clip to the **Normalize** row's target, measured through everything above as the export plays it. It's checked by rendering, to within 0.1 LU, up to three times.
78	
79	The target is used even when the row is set to Peak and the field is greyed out. Enhance Voice always aims at a loudness.
80	
81	## What it leaves alone
82	
83	Hum removal, the channel choice, pan, mono, fades, ducking, **Mute**, **Keep pitch** and the EQ's other parts all stay as they are. Like Normalize, it writes the clip's base settings, even with the playhead inside an action.
84	
85	## Clips Enhance Voice skips
86	
87	It's offered where [Normalize](/audio/normalize/#clips-normalize-skips) is, and it leaves out the same clips as Normalize in Loudness mode, plus two more. The rest of the selection is still enhanced. With nothing to enhance, the press beeps, and neither the button nor the menu says why.
88	
89	| Skipped | Why |
90	| --- | --- |
91	| A clip that plays no sound, or a nest | There's no voice of its own to measure. Open a nest to enhance the clips inside. |
92	| A clip that plays for under 0.4 s | It's too short for a loudness measurement. |
93	| A clip quieter than −70 LUFS, before or after its processing | There's no voice to work with. |
94	| A clip with under 1 second of speech | There's too little to measure a voice from. |
95	| A clip not analysed yet | See [Wait for analysis](#wait-for-analysis). |
96	| A clip whose reversed copy is still being made | It can't be rendered yet. |
97	| A clip whose processing can't be rendered | There's nothing to measure. |
98	
99	## Wait for analysis
100	
101	Enhance Voice needs two results that are worked out on your Mac after a file is imported: the clip's loudness and its speech. A clip without both yet is skipped, which often happens straight after an import. The **Loudness** readout says "measuring…" while the loudness is still running. Wait a moment and press again.
102	
103	## Check its gate by ear
104	
105	Enhance Voice sets the gate from the pauses it measured. On a voice with very soft word starts, the gate can bite into them, so listen to those words and lower the [gate](/audio/gate/)'s threshold if you need to.
106	
107	## Good to know
108	
109	- Applying the rumble cut also takes the EQ out of bypass if you'd bypassed it.
110	- Every clip it enhances ends up with its limiter on, because the volume is solved through it.
111	- Measuring takes time in proportion to the clip's length, and it waits for the clip's voice isolation to render first.
112	- Two clips in a selection can end up with different settings, because each is measured on its own.
113	
114	## With an agent
115	
116	`enhance_voice` takes its own target rather than the **Normalize** row's. It reports what it measured for each clip, exactly which settings it wrote, and one sentence per rule saying why, so an agent can tell you what the button doesn't. Each skipped clip comes back with its reason. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/#enhance_voice).
117

122	- [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
123	- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)

2	title: "Match Audio"
3	description: "Give several clips the loudness and speech tone of one of them, so takes from different microphones or rooms sit together, in one undo step."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Match Audio makes selected clips sound like one of them, the reference. It sets each other clip's loudness and speech tone in one undo step, which helps when two takes came from different microphones or rooms.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Match Audio…"
13	  tools="match_audio"
14	  needs="Nothing. Speech detection runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Match clips to a reference
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the clips, including the one that already sounds right. You need at least two clips that could play sound. A nest clip or a clip with no sound doesn't count, and with fewer than two the menu item is greyed out.
22	
23	2. Choose **Clip ▸ Match Audio…**.
24	
25	3. In **Match to:**, choose the reference.
26	
27	4. Leave **Loudness** and **EQ** ticked, or untick the one you don't want. **Match** is greyed out with both off.
28	
29	5. Choose **Match**.
30	
31	</Steps>
32	
33	The Measuring Sound sheet stays up while each clip is measured, which takes a moment on a long clip. It counts "Clip 1 of 3…" as it goes. Nothing changes until every clip is measured, and **Cancel** leaves everything as it is.
34	
35	When it finishes, the change is one undo step called "Match Audio". The results are ordinary settings in the [Volume](/audio/volume/), [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) and [EQ](/audio/eq/) sections, so you can adjust them afterwards.
36	
37	The sheet opens with both boxes ticked and the first clip chosen every time. It doesn't remember your last choice.
38	
39	## Choose the reference
40	
41	**Match to:** lists the clips in timeline order, by start time and then by track, and the first is chosen. Each row reads `name — track — m:ss (clip id)`, for example `Interview — Track 1 — 0:42 (clip 12)`, so you can tell two clips with the same name apart.
42	
43	The reference itself isn't changed. Frame Job measures it once as it sounds in the timeline: through its own settings, its limiter and its volume, but without its fades, ducking or Mute. Its loudness at that point is the target for the other clips.
44	
45	## What Loudness sets
46	
47	**Loudness** runs [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode on each other clip, with the reference's loudness as the target. It sets the clip's volume, measured through the clip's settings as they'll be after the match. When the clip's peaks would pass −1 dBTP at that loudness, it also sets the clip's limiter at that ceiling.
48	
49	A clip so quiet that it needs more than the volume's ceiling of 32× stops there and ends up quieter than the reference.
50	
51	Loudness doesn't need speech, so you can use it on music by unticking **EQ**.
52	
53	## What EQ sets
54	
55	**EQ** gives each other clip the tone of the reference's voice. Frame Job compares the average spectrum of each clip's speech with the reference's, in 23 third-octave bands from 79 Hz to 12.7 kHz. Only speech counts. Frame Job uses the speech saved for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) if the clip has any, and otherwise what speech detection found in the file. A clip needs about a second of speech.
56	
57	Each clip is measured with its EQ's shelves and bands off. The difference, less the overall level, is then fitted with the EQ's low shelf, three bands and high shelf:
58	
59	- Each gain stays within ±12 dB.
60	- Each band's Q stays between 0.5 and 4.
61	- A band is only used where the difference is at least 0.5 dB.
62	
63	Those five parts replace the clip's own. Its high-pass, low-pass and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/) stay as they were, and **Bypass** is turned off.
64	
65	## What stays the same
66	
67	Match Audio changes only the volume, limiter and EQ. Every other section, the fades, ducking, pan and Mute are left alone.
68	
69	Choosing **Match** again with the same choice changes nothing. Frame Job beeps and adds no undo step.
70	
71	## When a clip can't be matched
72	
73	A clip that can't be matched is skipped, and the others are still matched. No message names a skipped clip, so if one sounds unchanged, check it against the list below.
74	
75	If the reference can't be used, or nothing can be matched, Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and puts the reason at the foot of the inspector. When the reference is the problem, the message starts "The reference, clip 12,". When every clip fails, it starts "Nothing could be matched." and gives each clip's reason.
76	
77	| The reason says | What it means | What to do |
78	| --- | --- | --- |
79	| "is still being analysed — its loudness has not been measured yet" | Frame Job hasn't finished with the file, which often happens straight after an import. | Try again in a moment. |
80	| "is still being analysed — its speech has not been detected yet" | The same, for speech. This only applies with **EQ** on. | Try again in a moment, or untick **EQ**. |
81	| "plays no sound in this timeline" | Nothing from this clip reaches the mix. | Choose another clip. |
82	| "plays for under 0.4 s" | The clip is too short to have a loudness. | Choose a longer clip, or trim this one longer. |
83	| "is under −70 LUFS" | There's no sound to match. | Choose another clip. |
84	| "has under 1 s of speech" | The part that plays has too little speech to measure a tone. | Untick **EQ**, or choose a clip with more speech. |
85	| "has under 12 third-octave bands within 50 dB of its loudest" | The reference's sound is too narrow to match a tone to. | Choose another reference, or untick **EQ**. |
86	| "shares under 12 third-octave bands with the reference" | This clip and the reference have too little of the spectrum in common. | Match this clip again with **EQ** unticked. |
87	
88	If the project changes while the clips are being measured, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps, and the foot of the inspector says "the project changed while its sound was being measured, so nothing changed. Choose Match Audio again."
89	
90	## Good to know
91	
92	- Match Audio matches the average tone of speech. It doesn't match the room, reverb, noise or dynamics. For those, see [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/), [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/).
93	- You match to a clip, not to a track or a whole mix. To bring clips to a loudness you choose rather than to one another, use [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).
94	- Like Normalize, it changes each clip's own settings even with an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected. The action itself stays as it was.
95	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, it works on the clips inside the nest.
96	
97	## With an agent
98	
99	`match_audio` takes the reference and the clips directly, with no sheet. Unlike the menu, it reports what happened to each clip: the settings it changed, the loudness figures, how closely the EQ fits, and each skipped clip with its reason. The call can take seconds on a long clip. A nest can't be matched or used as the reference, the call fails if Loudness and EQ are both off, and a second identical call reports "Match Audio made no change". See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/#match_audio).
100

8	Every clip with sound is mixed by its own settings and then by its track's. This page is the map: where sound lives, the order it's processed in, and which page covers each job.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where={['The timeline', 'Clip tab ▸ Sound', 'The track header']}

13	/>
14	
15	## One kind of track for all sound
16	
17	Frame Job has no separate audio tracks. Any track can hold a clip with sound:
18	
19	- a video file
20	- an audio-only file, such as a voice-over, music or a recorder's take
21	- a microphone recording
22	- a clip split off with [Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
23	- a [nest](/editing/nests/) that holds sound
24	
25	Each clip has its own processing on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/). Each track can be [muted or soloed](/audio/mute-and-solo/) and has its own [volume and pan](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/), [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
26	
27	The preview and the export use the same mix, so what you hear while editing is what gets written. There are two exceptions:
28	
29	- The exported mix also passes through a master limiter the preview doesn't have, which holds its peaks under −1 dBTP unless an agent asks for another ceiling. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
30	- A track's compressor and limiter are exact in an export and approximate in the preview. See [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
31	
32	## Clip waveforms
33	
34	A clip with sound shows its waveform in the timeline, below the filmstrip when it has both. The waveform is the file's own level, so moving the **Volume** slider doesn't redraw it. The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) over it shows what you actually hear. A nest clip draws no waveform, because it has no file of its own.
35	
36	The waveform is drawn faded when the clip is muted, when its track is muted, or when another track's solo silences it. A track holding only sound clips is drawn as a shorter lane than a track with pictures. [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/) covers everything a clip draws.
37	
38	## The fixed signal order
39	
40	Sound passes through a clip's settings in one fixed order. You can't rearrange it. The order matters because each stage hears what the one before it left: the compressor's threshold, for example, is read against sound the noise reducer has already cleaned.
41	
42	1. [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
43	2. [Voice Effect](/audio/voice-effects/)
44	3. [Channels](/audio/channels/)
45	4. [EQ](/audio/eq/)
46	5. [Hum](/audio/hum-removal/)
47	6. [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
48	7. [Gate](/audio/gate/)
49	8. [Leveller](/audio/leveller/)
50	9. [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/)
51	10. [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)
52	11. [Mix](/audio/pan-and-mono/): Mix to mono, then Pan
53	12. [Limiter](/audio/limiter/)
54	13. [Volume](/audio/volume/), [fades](/audio/fades/) and [ducking](/audio/ducking/)
55	
56	The last step works like a fader. Those three are the first sections on the Sound tab, because they're what you reach for most, but they're applied last. The other sections read down the tab in signal order.
57	
58	The limiter takes the clip's **Volume** into account, so its ceiling holds at the level you set, even though Volume comes after it in the list.
59	
60	## Sound on a nest
61	
62	A nest clip has the same Sound tab, but most of the controls don't reach the clips inside it.
63	
64	| On a nest clip | What it does |
65	| --- | --- |
66	| **Volume**, **Mute** and the fades | Scale everything inside. Turning a nest down turns all of it down, and muting it silences all of it. |
67	| **Mix to mono** | Folds the nest's whole mix. Pans on the tracks inside it no longer apply. |
68	| **Ducking** | Lowers everything for the nest's whole length, the clips inside it included. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/#good-to-know). |
69	| Pan, Channels, EQ, Hum, Gate, Leveller, De-esser, Compressor, Voice Isolation, Voice Effect, Noise Reduction and Limiter | Nothing. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set them on the clips inside. |
70	
71	A nest clip draws no [volume line](/audio/volume-line/), and [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) pass over it, because its level lives in the clips inside. Alone in the selection it leaves both buttons disabled. Beside an ordinary clip, the ordinary clip is processed and the nest is skipped.
72	
73	## What a track adds
74	
75	A track acts as a bus, one shared channel for all its clips. Its volume, compressor and limiter work on everything on it, after each clip's own settings. Its pan works on everything on it too, right before each clip's Limiter, so a limited clip still holds its ceiling.
76	
77	A clip inside a nest plays through its own track in the nest and then through the track the nest clip sits on. Track volumes and pans multiply along the way, so a clip panned left on a track panned left leans further left. A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter, only volume and pan.
78	
79	## Sound analysis after import
80	
81	Frame Job analyses each file's sound on your Mac after import, with no key and no upload: first its waveform, then its loudness, then what Synchronize Audio matches on, and then where its speech is. Until that finishes:
82	
83	- The clip has no waveform yet.
84	- The **Loudness** readout says "measuring…".
85	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) skip the clip.
86	- [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) skips it, and if that leaves nothing to match, it says the clip "is still being analysed".
87	- [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) stops and says the clip "is still being analysed".
88	
89	Try again in a moment. Nothing needs starting by hand.
90	
91	## Find the right tool
92	
93	| To | Use |
94	| --- | --- |
95	| Set how loud a clip plays | [Clip volume](/audio/volume/) |
96	| Change the level over time | [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/) or [actions](/audio/animate-sound/) |
97	| Bring clips to one loudness | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
98	| Clean up a voice recording in one step | [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) |
99	| Make one clip sound like another | [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) |
100	| Drop the music under a voice | [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) or [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/) |
101	| Line up a camera and a separate recorder | [Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) |
102	| Move sound to its own clip, or make a J-cut | [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/), [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/) |
103	| Give many clips the same treatment | [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/) copies the whole sound setup in one step |
104	| Cut out dead air | [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) |
105	| Check a mix by ear and by number | [The level meter](/audio/level-meter/) and [the Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) |
106

2	title: "The Sound tab"
3	description: The Clip tab's Sound sub-tab, its fifteen sections, and how to read, reset and edit them across several clips.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	The Sound tab is where you set how a clip plays: how loud it is, how it's cleaned up and where it sits in the mix.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound" tools={['set_audio', 'get_project']} />
12	
13	<Shot
14	  name="09-clip-sound.inspector"
15	  alt="The Clip tab with an audio file selected and the Sound sub-tab chosen. The Volume section is open, showing Volume at 100%, Gain +0.0 dB, Loudness and At volume both −21.8 LUFS · −20.8 dBTP, Mute, the Normalize row set to Loudness at −16 LUFS, and the Normalize and Enhance Voice buttons. Below it the Fades section reads none, and Ducking and Voice Isolation read off."
16	/>
17	
18	## When the tab appears
19	
20	The Clip tab shows **Sound** when the selection includes at least one clip that plays sound. That means a clip whose file has an audio track with its sound switched on, or a nest that holds audio. A clip whose sound is [switched off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) doesn't count.
21	
22	Click a clip on the timeline and the inspector moves to the **Clip** tab. An audio-only clip has no picture, so the tab opens straight on Sound. For a video clip, choose the **Sound** sub-tab.
23	
24	## The sections
25	
26	Each section header shows a one-line summary of its state, so you can read a clip's setup with every section closed. The summary is drawn a little stronger when the section differs from its default.
27	
28	| Section | What it's for | Its summary reads | **Reset** does |
29	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
30	| [Volume](/audio/volume/) | Level, readouts, Mute, Normalize and Enhance Voice | "muted", "silent" at 0 %, or the gain, such as "+3.5 dB" | Volume to 100 %, Mute off |
31	| [Fades](/audio/fades/) | Fade in and fade out | Both lengths, such as "0.50 · 1.00 s", or "none" | Both lengths to 0 |
32	| [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) | Lowers every other clip while this one plays | The level, such as "20%", or "off" | Turns it off |
33	| [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) | Keeps the voice, removes what's around it | The amount, such as "80%", or "off" | Turns it off |
34	| [Voice Effect](/audio/voice-effects/) | One of sixteen effects | The effect and amount, such as "Space: Hall 100%", or "off" | Turns it off |
35	| [Channels](/audio/channels/) | Which channels of a stereo file play | "Both", "Left Only", "Right Only" or "Swap Left and Right" | Back to Both |
36	| [EQ](/audio/eq/) | Shapes the tone | Parts switched on, such as "2 on", "bypassed", or "off" | Turns it off |
37	| [Hum](/audio/hum-removal/) | Removes mains hum and its harmonics | The mains and harmonics, such as "60 Hz · 4", or "off" | Turns it off |
38	| [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) | Lowers steady background noise | The amount, such as "50%", or "off" | Turns it off |
39	| [Gate](/audio/gate/) | Turns the pauses between phrases down | The threshold, such as "−10 dB", or "off" | Turns it off |
40	| [Leveller](/audio/leveller/) | Evens out a speaker who moves on and off the microphone | The target, such as "0 dB", or "off" | Turns it off |
41	| [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/) | Tames harsh "s" sounds | The frequency, such as "6.0 kHz", or "off" | Turns it off |
42	| [Compressor](/audio/compressor/) | Smooths the volume | The ratio, such as "3.0:1", or "off" | Turns it off |
43	| [Mix](/audio/pan-and-mono/) | Pan, Mix to mono, Detach Audio and Attach Audio | "centre", "mono", or the pan, such as "left 40" | Pan to centre, Mix to mono off |
44	| [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) | Holds the clip's peaks under a ceiling | The ceiling, such as "−1.0 dBTP", or "off" | Turns it off |
45	
46	Voice Isolation through Limiter are in the order sound passes through them. Volume, the fades and ducking apply last, like a fader. See [The fixed signal order](/audio/how-audio-works/#the-fixed-signal-order).
47	
48	Click a header to open or close its section. Every section starts closed, and Frame Job remembers what you open and close. If the tab would show nothing but closed headers, the first section you haven't closed yourself opens.
49	
50	## Reset a section
51	
52	Each header has a **Reset** button that appears when the section differs from its default. It's one undo step, and it reaches every selected clip.
53	
54	Two resets leave something behind:
55	
56	- **Reset** on Fades clears the two lengths and keeps **In shape** and **Out shape**.
57	- **Reset** on Volume leaves the Limiter alone, even one that Normalize turned on.
58	
59	With an [action selected](/motion/select-an-action/), a section that can animate shows **Clear** in the same place, while the action sets something in it. **Clear** removes the section from the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/).
60	
61	## Pick a common value
62	
63	Most number fields have a chevron at their right end that opens a short menu of common values, beside the slider and the typed field. The current value is ticked. For example:
64	
65	| Control | Quick picks |
66	| --- | --- |
67	| **Volume** | 0, 50, 100, 150, 200, 400 % |
68	| **Fade in** and **Fade out** | 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2 s |
69	| **Limiter** ▸ **Ceiling** | −1, −2, −3, −6 dBTP |
70	
71	A number you type is held to the control's range. See [Inspector fields](/getting-started/inspector-fields/).
72	
73	## Edit several clips at once
74	
75	Select the clips and change a control. The change goes to every selected clip that has sound, as one undo step. A control whose clips hold different values is marked **mixed**.
76	
77	The sections with a checkbox, such as Ducking and Compressor, work as one unit. Changing one of their controls gives every selected clip all of that section's values as the first clip has them, not only the value you changed.
78	
79	**Normalize** and **Enhance Voice** are the exceptions to one shared change. Each clip gets its own settings from its own measurement. The **Loudness** and **At volume** readouts show "—" with several clips selected, because they describe one clip.
80	
81	## With an agent
82	
83	`set_audio` changes any of these settings on one or more clips in one call, and `get_project` reads them back. An agent sends only what should change, and everything else stays as it is. A value out of range is turned down with a message naming it, not adjusted to fit. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#set_audio).
84	
85	`set_audio` always writes the clip's own settings. To [animate one](/audio/animate-sound/), an agent uses an action instead.
86

2	title: "Clip volume"
3	description: Set how loud a clip plays, mute it, and read its gain, loudness and true peak in the Volume section.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	The Volume section sets a clip's level and tells you how loud the clip is before and after that level. It's the first section on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Volume" tools={['set_audio', 'normalize_clip']} />
12	
13	<Shot
14	  name="09-clip-sound.inspector"
15	  alt="The Volume section open on the Sound tab: the Volume slider and a field at 100%, Gain +0.0 dB, Loudness and At volume both −21.8 LUFS · −20.8 dBTP, an unticked Mute box, the Normalize row, and the Normalize and Enhance Voice buttons."
16	/>
17	
18	## Set the volume
19	
20	Select the clip and open the **Volume** section. Drag the **Volume** slider, type in its field, or choose a value from the field's chevron: 0, 50, 100, 150, 200 or 400 %.
21	
22	| Control | Default | Range |
23	| --- | --- | --- |
24	| **Volume** | 100 % | 0 to 3200 % (+30.1 dB) |
25	
26	The slider stops at 400 %. To go higher, type in the field, up to 3200 %. Above 400 % the slider's knob stays at the right end. The high ceiling is there so that a quiet microphone recording can be brought up.
27	
28	To change the level partway through a clip, [add a point](/audio/volume-line/#add-a-point) on the volume line. With an [action selected](/audio/animate-sound/), **Volume** writes the level the action ends on, not the clip's own.
29	
30	## Mute a clip
31	
32	Tick **Mute** to silence the clip without changing its volume. It's off by default.
33	
34	A muted clip's waveform is drawn faded and its [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) lies along the bottom. To silence a whole track, use [Mute and solo tracks](/audio/mute-and-solo/).
35	
36	With an action selected, **Mute** switches at the action's end, and the row shows "at end".
37	
38	## Read the level
39	
40	Three rows report the clip's level. You can't edit them.
41	
42	### Gain
43	
44	**Gain** is the **Volume** in decibels, such as "+3.0 dB", or "silent" at 0 %. At 100 % it reads "+0.0 dB".
45	
46	### Loudness
47	
48	**Loudness** is the clip's integrated loudness and true peak at volume 100 %, such as "−41.7 LUFS · −18.5 dBTP". It's measured to BS.1770-4 over the part of the file the clip plays.
49	
50	On a stereo file, the reading includes the channel choice, Mix to mono and Pan. A mono clip counts as dual mono, as an export plays it, which reads about 3 dB louder than the file alone.
51	
52	It leaves out **Volume**, fades, ducking, **Mute** and solo, the track's volume, and EQ, Hum and the rest of the clip's processing.
53	
54	A clip at another speed, or a ramped one, reads within about 0.5 LU of what plays. A file with more than two channels is measured from a two-channel mix of it.
55	
56	### At volume
57	
58	**At volume** is the same reading with the clip's **Volume** applied, and through its [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) when that's on. With the limiter on, the true peak reads no higher than the ceiling. The row follows a **Volume** drag as you move.
59	
60	The fast reading can't hear EQ, Hum, Voice Isolation, Noise Reduction, the Gate, the Leveller, the De-esser, the Compressor or a Voice Effect. On a clip using any of them:
61	
62	- If [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode or [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) has measured the clip as it is now, the row reads that measurement.
63	- Otherwise the figure is the one before the processing and starts with "≈". Its tooltip says so.
64	
65	**At volume** doesn't measure on its own, so "≈" stays until you press one of those two.
66	
67	### What the readouts can show instead
68	
69	| It reads | Because |
70	| --- | --- |
71	| "measuring…" | The clip's [sound analysis](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-analysis-after-import) hasn't finished. |
72	| "—" | Several clips are selected, or a nest is, or the clip can't be measured. |
73	| "— LUFS" beside a peak | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, or it's quieter than −70 LUFS throughout. |
74	| "silent" (At volume) | **Volume** is 0 %. |
75	
76	## Reset the section
77	
78	**Reset** in the section's header puts **Volume** back to 100 % and turns **Mute** off. It leaves the Normalize row alone, and it leaves the [Limiter](/audio/limiter/) alone, including one Normalize turned on.
79	
80	## Good to know
81	
82	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) sit at the bottom of this section. Both set **Volume** for you, and both leave **Mute** alone.
83	- On a [nest clip](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-on-a-nest), **Volume** and **Mute** scale everything inside it.
84	- A muted clip that ducks still lowers the others. See [Ducking](/audio/ducking/).
85

2	title: "The volume line"
3	description: See a clip's level over time on the timeline, drag it, and add points to shape it.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The volume line is the thin white line over a clip's waveform. It shows how loud that clip plays over time, and you can drag it to change the level without leaving the timeline.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  keys="⌥-click"
13	  where="On a clip's audio part in the timeline"
14	  tools={['set_audio', 'add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_action']}
15	/>
16	
17	## The line on a clip
18	
19	Every clip with sound draws the line, except a nest clip. It's the level you hear from that clip, with everything that shapes it folded in:
20	
21	- the clip's **Volume** and its volume actions
22	- its fades and crossfades
23	- ducking from other clips
24	- the track's volume
25	
26	The top of the clip's audio part is +30 dB (3200 %) and the bottom is −60 dB or quieter. A clip at 100 % sits about a third of the way down.
27	
28	A clip you can't hear has its line along the bottom. That's a muted clip, one on a muted track, or one silenced by another track's solo.
29	
30	A small square in the action colour marks each action end that sets the volume. Those squares are the line's points.
31	
32	The line starts below the [action lane](/motion/action-lane/) and is only drawn where the audio part is at least 12 pt tall, so at the Small [track height](/timeline/track-height/) it may not show.
33	
34	## Drag the line
35	
36	Press within 3 pt of the line and drag up or down. The press selects the clip. The new level appears beside the pointer, such as "+2.5 dB", or "−∞ dB" at silence. One drag is one undo step, "Set Volume".
37	
38	What the drag changes depends on where you press:
39	
40	| You press | The drag changes |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| Inside an action that sets the volume | That action's end level |
43	| After such an action | The end level of the last one before the point |
44	| Anywhere else | The clip's own **Volume** |
45	
46	The drag is vertical only and relative to where you pressed. It moves in decibels, and it covers the whole scale over the height of the audio part, so a taller [track](/timeline/track-height/) gives you finer control.
47	
48	To go to silence, drag down to the very bottom of the audio part. Upwards, the level stops at 3200 %.
49	
50	The readout is the level you're setting, not the sum on the line. The line includes track volume and ducking, but a drag changes only the clip's own level, so on a silenced clip the line stays on the floor while the readout changes.
51	
52	## Add a point
53	
54	A point lets the level change partway through a clip.
55	
56	<Steps>
57	
58	1. Hold <kbd>⌥</kbd> and click the line where you want the point.
59	
60	2. Keep the mouse down and drag to set its level, or let go and drag the line later.
61	
62	</Steps>
63	
64	A point is an [action](/motion/actions/), not a keyframe. Frame Job adds an action running from the end of the previous action, or the clip's start, up to where you clicked, ending at the volume the clip already has there. The click on its own changes nothing you hear. It's one undo step, "Add Volume Point".
65	
66	Inside an action that changes only the volume, the click splits that action in two at the point. Both halves keep its curve, so a linear action sounds the same until you drag, and an eased one eases again on each side of the point.
67	
68	The click beeps and adds nothing:
69	
70	- inside an action that doesn't set the volume, or that changes anything else as well
71	- inside an action that runs past the clip's end, as one can after a trim
72	- within one frame of the clip's start, the start of the action it's in, or the previous action's end
73	
74	## Move or remove a point
75	
76	To move a point in time, drag its action band. To remove one, select the band and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. See [Move, resize or remove an action](/motion/change-an-action/).
77	
78	## Clicks that reach the clip instead
79	
80	Some presses on the line act on the clip, as they do anywhere else on it:
81	
82	| Press | What it does |
83	| --- | --- |
84	| <kbd>⇧</kbd>-click | Adds the clip to the selection or takes it out |
85	| <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd>-drag | Slips the clip |
86	| Double-click | Renames the clip |
87	
88	The fade handles, the action lane and the clip's edges take a press before the line does.
89	
90	## Good to know
91	
92	- The line doesn't respond on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/).
93	- A clip with its [sound switched off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/) draws no line, and neither does one playing [too fast to have sound](/speed/sound-at-high-speed/).
94	- Inside an open nest, the line is the nest's own mix. It doesn't include the volume, fades, mute or solo of the nest clip and the tracks outside it.
95	
96	## With an agent
97	
98	There's no separate tool for the line. A drag is `set_audio`, or `set_action_end` on the action that sets the level there, and a point is `add_action` then `set_action_end`, with `set_action` when it splits an action. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#volume-and-mute) and [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).
99

2	title: "Animate sound with actions"
3	description: Change a clip's sound over time with actions, from a pan sweep to an EQ that opens up, and what can't be animated.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	An [action](/motion/actions/) can change a clip's sound as it plays: a pan sweeps across, an EQ band rises, the isolated voice fades in. What you hear in the preview is what an export writes.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
13	  keys="⌥⌘K"
14	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound, with an action selected"
15	  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end']}
16	/>
17	
18	## Animate a sound setting
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Select the clip, move the playhead to where the change should start, and [add an action](/motion/add-an-action/) with <kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>. The new action lasts 1 second and is already selected.
23	
24	2. Open the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
25	
26	3. Set the controls to how they should be when the action ends.
27	
28	4. To make the change take longer, [drag the end of the action's band](/motion/change-an-action/).
29	
30	</Steps>
31	
32	To come back to an action later, [select it](/motion/select-an-action/) first. Otherwise the Sound tab changes the clip's own settings.
33	
34	For the level alone, it's quicker to <kbd>⌥</kbd>-click the [volume line](/audio/volume-line/#add-a-point).
35	
36	## What an action can animate
37	
38	With an action selected, these write that action's end state instead of the clip's own settings:
39	
40	- **Volume**, **Mute** and the fade lengths
41	- **Pan** and **Mix to mono**
42	- **Channels**
43	- the **EQ** and **Hum**
44	- **Amount** in Voice Isolation
45	- **Noise Reduction**
46	- the **Gate**, the **Leveller** and the **De-esser**
47	- the **Compressor** and the **Limiter**
48	
49	## Numbers glide, switches jump
50	
51	Numbers move smoothly across the action's span. Switches hold their start value and change at the action's end, with no glide, as at a cut between two clips.
52	
53	These are the switches:
54	
55	- **Mute**, **Mix to mono** and **EQ** Bypass
56	- turning a section or an EQ slot on or off
57	- **Channels**
58	- a pass filter's slope
59	- **Hum**'s mains and harmonics
60	- the **Leveller**'s Response
61	
62	Unticking a section or an EQ slot with an action selected turns it off at the action's end.
63	
64	A number only glides while its section is on at both ends of the action. A section an action turns on arrives at its end values when the action ends. Voice Isolation's **Amount** and Noise Reduction's **Remove noise** are the exceptions. Each is one amount, and 0 is its off, so it glides up from 0 or down to it.
65	
66	## What can't be animated
67	
68	These always change the clip's own settings, even with an action selected:
69	
70	- **Ducking**
71	- **Keep pitch**
72	- the fade shapes, **In shape** and **Out shape**
73	- the **Voice Effect**
74	- a nest clip's **Mix to mono**
75	
76	A row like this shows ⊘ in front of its label while an action is selected. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
77	
78	A voice effect is made from the clip's own Voice Isolation **Amount**, not an animated one.
79	
80	[Normalize](/audio/normalize/), [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) also write the clip's own settings with an action selected. The **Normalize** button carries a small boxed "clip" tag to show this.
81	
82	## Processing turned on by an action
83	
84	A clip gets whatever preparation its sound needs when an action asks for it, even if the clip's own setting is off:
85	
86	- The isolated voice is made when an action raises **Amount**, on a clip whose own Voice Isolation is off.
87	- The Gate, the Leveller and the De-esser measure the clip's loudness when an action turns them on.
88	- A Limiter or Noise Reduction turned on by an action is set up for the clip's whole track, as one set on the clip itself is, so the sound's timing doesn't shift at the moment it comes on.
89	
90	## With an agent
91	
92	`set_audio` only reaches a clip's own settings. To animate, an agent uses `add_action` and then `set_action_end`. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#set_action_end).
93	
94	## Related
95

97	- [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/)
98	- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
99	- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)

1	---
2	title: "Audio fades"
3	description: Fade a clip's sound in and out from the inspector or the handles on the clip, and choose the shape of each fade.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	A fade brings a clip's sound up from silence at its start or down to silence at its end, so it doesn't begin or stop abruptly. Fades change the sound only.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  where={['Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Fades', 'The fade handles on a clip']}
12	  tools="set_audio"
13	/>
14	
15	## Set a fade length
16	
17	Open the **Fades** section on the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/) and set the lengths.
18	
19	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
20	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
21	| **Fade in** | How long the sound takes to rise from silence at the clip's start. | 0 | 0 to 10 s |
22	| **Fade out** | How long the sound takes to fall to silence at the clip's end. | 0 | 0 to 10 s |
23	
24	The field's chevron offers 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 s. A length you type here is kept exactly as typed, not rounded to whole frames.
25	
26	The section's summary shows both lengths, such as "0.50 · 1.00 s", or "none". **Reset** clears both lengths and leaves the shapes as they are.
27	
28	With an [action selected](/audio/animate-sound/), these two rows write the action's end state.
29	
30	## Drag a fade handle
31	
32	Every clip with sound has a small square handle at each top corner of its audio part. Drag the left handle inward to set the fade in, or the right handle inward to set the fade out. The handle then sits at the end of the fade.
33	
34	The handles and the inspector rows change the same two settings, with these differences:
35	
36	- A handle's length snaps to whole frames.
37	- A handle can go past 10 s, up to the length of the clip. The 10 s limit is the inspector's.
38	- A handle changes that one clip, not the whole selection, and it doesn't select the clip.
39	- A handle changes the clip's own fade, even with an action selected.
40	
41	Each drag is one undo step, "Set Fade". Handles don't snap to clip edges, markers or the playhead, because a fade is a length, not a position.
42	
43	Handles don't respond on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/). They aren't drawn when the clip's audio part is under 10 pt tall.
44	
45	## Choose a fade shape
46	
47	**In shape** and **Out shape** set how the level moves across each fade. The default for both is **Linear**.
48	
49	| Shape | On a fade in | On a fade out | Level halfway |
50	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
51	| **Linear** | A straight ramp, the same amount every moment. | The same in reverse. | 50 % |
52	| **S-Curve** | Starts and ends gently, moving fastest in the middle. | The same. | 50 % |
53	| **+3 dB** | Rises quickly, then levels off. Good for a fade in that should be heard straight away. | Holds up, then falls quickly at the end. | 71 %, 3 dB under full |
54	| **−3 dB** | Starts slowly and gathers speed. | Falls quickly, then trails away. Good for a fade out that should feel long. | 29 %, about 11 dB under full |
55	
56	The shapes always belong to the clip itself. With an action selected they're marked ⊘ and still change the clip's own setting, and an action can't [animate](/audio/animate-sound/#what-cant-be-animated) them.
57	
58	A crossfade between two clips has its own shape, with the same four choices. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/).
59	
60	## When a clip moves or is trimmed
61	
62	A fade is measured from the clip's own edges:
63	
64	- **Move** a clip and the fade travels with it.
65	- **Trim** a clip and the fade stays at the edge, the same length.
66	- **Split** a clip and both halves keep both fade lengths, so a fade in also starts the second half and a fade out also ends the first.
67	
68	Where a fade in and a fade out overlap, the two multiply. That gives a dip in the middle rather than a jump. A length you type can be longer than the clip, and that fade is then cut off at the clip's other edge, so the sound never reaches full level.
69	
70	## Good to know
71	
72	- On a [nest clip](/audio/how-audio-works/#sound-on-a-nest), fades scale everything inside the nest.
73	- The [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) shows a clip's fades, so you can see them against the level.
74	
75	## With an agent
76	
77	`set_audio` sets a fade's length and shape on one or more clips, with `fade_in`, `fade_out`, `fade_in_shape` and `fade_out_shape`. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#fades-and-fade-shapes). A crossfade is set with `set_transition_style` instead. See [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/).
78	
79	## Related
80	
81	- [Crossfades](/audio/crossfades/)
82	- [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/)
83	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)

1	---
2	title: "Crossfades"
3	description: "Fade one clip's sound into the next across a transition, choose the shape of the fade, and crossfade clips that have no picture."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	When two clips on a track overlap with a transition, the transition can fade the outgoing sound out and the incoming sound in, so the cut isn't heard as a jump.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Clip sub-tab ▸ Transition section"
13	  tools="set_transition_style"
14	/>
15	
16	## Crossfade audio
17	
18	A new transition already crossfades its sound, at the **+3 dB** shape, so most of the time there's nothing to do. Open the section to turn the crossfade off, or to change its shape.
19	
20	<Steps>
21	
22	1. Select the later of the two overlapping clips, on its own. The **Transition** section only appears for a single clip that overlaps the clip before it.
23	
24	2. In the Clip tab, choose the **Clip** sub-tab and open **Transition**.
25	
26	3. Tick or untick **Crossfade Audio**.
27	
28	</Steps>
29	
30	| **Crossfade Audio** | What you hear across the overlap |
31	| --- | --- |
32	| On | The outgoing sound fades out and the incoming sound fades in. If only one of the two clips has sound, that clip still fades. |
33	| Off | Both clips play at their own level for the whole overlap, mixed together. |
34	
35	The fade follows the transition's **Curve**, so an eased transition eases its sound too. A new transition is **Ease In Out**. **Curve** and **Crossfade Audio** are separate settings, and changing one leaves the other alone.
36	
37	To change the overlap's length, use the **Duration** row. See [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/).
38	
39	## Choose a crossfade shape
40	
41	**Crossfade Shape** sets the curve of the fade. It's available while **Crossfade Audio** is on, and the default is **+3 dB**. The incoming clip follows the shape, and the outgoing clip follows it in reverse.
42	
43	| **Crossfade Shape** | What it does | Each clip's level halfway through the fade |
44	| --- | --- | --- |
45	| **Linear** | A straight-line pair. It dips 3 dB in the middle of two unrelated takes, but suits two parts of the same sound. | About −6 dB |
46	| **S-Curve** | A fade that does most of its changing in the middle of the overlap and moves slowly at both ends. | About −6 dB |
47	| **+3 dB** | Constant power, which holds the level steady across two unrelated takes. | About −3 dB |
48	| **−3 dB** | A slow start. The incoming sound rises late and the outgoing sound falls early, so the middle of the overlap is the quietest of the four. | About −11 dB |
49	
50	## Audio-only transitions
51	
52	Two overlapping clips with no picture get the same **Transition** section, on the same sub-tab. Only their sound changes. **Crossfade Audio**, **Crossfade Shape** and **Curve** control the fade, **Duration** sets its length, and **Kind** has no visible effect.
53	
54	Whenever an edit makes a clip overlap the one before it, Frame Job adds a transition, for audio clips as for any other. So overlapping two music clips crossfades them straight away. See [Add or remove a transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) for the other ways to make one.
55	
56	## Crossfade after Detach Audio
57	
58	[Detach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/) moves a clip's sound to its own clip on the track below and switches it off on the picture clip, so **Crossfade Audio** on the transition between two picture clips no longer fades that sound. The fade belongs to the detached audio clips instead.
59	
60	Detach both clips of an overlap and their audio clips overlap on that track, which gives them a transition of their own that crossfades them. Audio clips that don't overlap yet get one as soon as you overlap them. Select the later audio clip to change it.
61	
62	## Good to know
63	
64	- The crossfade multiplies whatever else is happening to the sound. Mute, solo, ducking, volume and a clip's own fades still apply on top.
65	- With **Kind** set to **None**, an overlap has no transition of its own. It plays as a linear cross dissolve with no sound crossfade, and the section shows **Linear** and **Crossfade Audio** off. Changing either of them gives the overlap a transition with exactly the values shown.
66	- Choosing another style from **Clip ▸ Transition** on a clip that already has a transition keeps its curve and its crossfade.
67	- A transition on a nest clip fades all the sound inside the nest. A crossfade between clips inside the nest still happens too, and you hear both.
68	- Each clip's [limiter](/audio/limiter/) holds that clip alone, so two limited clips can add up past the ceiling during an overlap. An export's master limiter catches this, but the preview has none, so it can sound louder while you edit. A [track compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) is also approximate in the preview where clips overlap.
69	
70	## With an agent
71	
72	`set_transition_style` sets the crossfade with `audio` (true or false) and its shape with `audio_shape`: `plus_3db`, `linear`, `s_curve` or `minus_3db`. A key you leave out keeps what's there. See [Tools: transitions](/mcp/tools-transitions/#set_transition_style).
73	
74	## Related
75	
76	- [The Transition section](/motion/transition-settings/)
77	- [Audio fades](/audio/fades/)
78	- [Detach and Attach Audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/)
79	- [J-cuts and L-cuts](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/)
