1	---
2	title: Voice effects
3	description: Give a clip's sound one of sixteen effects, from a pitch shift or a phone line to a cathedral, and set how much of it you hear.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Voice Effect changes the character of a clip's sound: pitch a voice up or down, squeeze it into a phone line, or put it in a hall. A clip has one effect at a time.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect"
13	  tools="set_audio"
14	  needs="Nothing. Apple's audio units render the effect on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Choose an effect
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
22	
23	2. Open the **Voice Effect** section.
24	
25	3. Choose an effect from **Effect**. The list names each one with its group, such as **Space: Hall**.
26	
27	4. Set [Amount](#set-the-amount), and [Pitch](#set-the-pitch) for the three effects that use it.
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	Frame Job renders the effect in the background, and you hear it [when that's done](#when-you-hear-the-effect). Each effect keeps the clip at about the loudness it had, so switching between them doesn't jump in level.
32	
33	To take the effect off, choose **None**, or choose **Reset** in the section's header. The header shows the effect and its amount, such as "Space: Hall 100%", or "off".
34	
35	With several clips selected, a change applies to all of them. **Amount** and **Pitch** give every selected clip the first clip's whole effect, not only the value you changed. See [Edit several clips at once](/audio/sound-tab/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
36	
37	## The effects
38	
39	The figures here are at an Amount of 100 %.
40	
41	### Voice
42	
43	| Effect | What it does |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| **Voice: Pitch** | Shifts the voice up or down without changing its speed. It starts at 0 semitones, so it changes nothing until you set [Pitch](#set-the-pitch). |
46	| **Voice: High** | Shifts the voice up 5 semitones, cuts the lows below 150 Hz and lifts the highs above 4 kHz by 3 dB, for a small, high voice. |
47	| **Voice: Deep** | Shifts the voice down 5 semitones, adds 4 dB of low weight below 150 Hz and takes 3 dB off the highs above 5 kHz. |
48	| **Voice: Robot** | Makes the voice metallic and buzzing, with a 60 Hz ring modulator and a short 8 ms delay. |
49	
50	### Tone
51	
52	| Effect | What it does |
53	| --- | --- |
54	| **Tone: Bass** | Boosts the lows below 200 Hz by 10 dB. |
55	| **Tone: Treble** | Boosts the highs above 3 kHz by 10 dB. |
56	| **Tone: Bright** | Lifts the presence with 4 dB around 3 kHz, and the air with 6 dB above 8 kHz. |
57	| **Tone: Telephone** | Squeezes the sound into the narrow band of a phone line, 300 Hz to 3.4 kHz. |
58	| **Tone: Radio** | Squeezes the sound into 400 Hz to 4.5 kHz and adds a radio tower's crackle. |
59	
60	### Character
61	
62	| Effect | What it does |
63	| --- | --- |
64	| **Character: Lo-Fi** | Limits the sound to 150 Hz to 6 kHz and crushes it, so it's gritty and dull, like a low-resolution recording. |
65	| **Character: Distorted** | Overdrives the sound into heavy distortion. |
66	
67	### Space
68	
69	| Effect | What it does |
70	| --- | --- |
71	| **Space: Echo** | Repeats the sound every quarter of a second, each repeat darkened above 6 kHz. |
72	| **Space: Room** | Puts the sound in a medium room, with a 35 % reverb mix. |
73	| **Space: Hall** | Puts the sound in a large hall, with a 40 % reverb mix. |
74	| **Space: Plate** | Adds a plate reverb, with a 35 % mix. |
75	| **Space: Cathedral** | Puts the sound in a cathedral with a long tail, with a 45 % reverb mix. |
76	
77	## Set the amount
78	
79	**Amount** is how much of the effect you hear, from 0 to 100 %. It starts at 100 %, and its quick picks are 25, 50 and 100 %. It's greyed out until you choose an effect.
80	
81	Every boost, mix and shift scales with it, and the edges of a band move in from where they'd do nothing. At 50 %, **Voice: High** shifts 2.5 semitones and **Tone: Bass** boosts by 5 dB. At 0 the clip plays as it is.
82	
83	Choosing another effect keeps the Amount. Choosing **None** forgets it, so the next effect starts at 100 %.
84	
85	## Set the pitch
86	
87	**Pitch** is the shift in semitones, from −12 to 12. Its quick picks are −12, −5, 0, 5 and 12. It works only for **Voice: Pitch**, **Voice: High** and **Voice: Deep**, and it's greyed out for the rest.
88	
89	Choosing one of the three sets Pitch back to that effect's own: 0, +5 or −5. Amount scales the shift too, so a Pitch of 12 at an Amount of 50 % shifts by 6 semitones.
90	
91	## Read the status
92	
93	**Status** says where the effect's render has got to. With several clips selected it reads "—".
94	
95	| Status | What it means |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| Off | The clip has no effect, or one that changes nothing, such as an Amount of 0 or **Voice: Pitch** at 0 semitones. |
98	| Rendering… | The effect is being worked out. Until it's done the clip plays without it. |
99	| Ready | The clip plays with the effect. |
100	| Plays without it at this speed | The clip has a speed change, a speed ramp or a freeze frame. An effect plays only at normal speed. |
101	| Waits for the reversed copy | The clip is reversed and its [reversed copy](/speed/reverse/) isn't ready yet. |
102	| Not rendered: and a reason | The render failed. The reason might be "its media cannot be found" or "its isolated voice was not rendered". |
103	
104	## When you hear the effect
105	
106	The effect is worked out once for each clip, in the background. Until it's ready the clip plays without it, and the editor switches over by itself when it is. A clip that isn't at normal speed plays without the effect, and [Status](#read-the-status) says so.
107	
108	Changing the effect, Amount, Pitch or the clip's [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) amount works it out again. So does trimming or slipping the clip, because the clip then plays a different part of its file. Moving the clip along the timeline doesn't.
109	
110	An export waits for every clip's effect, and its sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name meanwhile, so a file is never written without one. If a render fails, the export stops and names the clip.
111	
112	## Where it sits in the chain
113	
114	The effect comes right after Voice Isolation and before everything else in the [Sound tab's order](/audio/how-audio-works/). An isolated clip's effect is made from its isolated voice, so it waits for that first. The channel choice, the EQ, noise reduction and the sections after them all work on the effected sound.
115	
116	## Good to know
117	
118	- A reverb or an echo stops at the end of the clip. It doesn't ring on into the next one.
119	- A clip split from a take starts its effect fresh at the cut, so a reverb or echo doesn't carry across the join.
120	- On a stereo file a reverb or an echo mixes the two channels together, so the [channel choice](/audio/channels/) picks from the effected pair, not from the original left and right.
121	- The effect can't be animated. Voice Effect is marked ⊘ inside an [action](/audio/animate-sound/), and a change there still applies to the whole clip. It's also made from the clip's own Voice Isolation amount, not an animated one.
122	- The waveform, the Loudness readout and [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) hear the clip without its effect. [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it, and waits for the render first.
123	- On a nest clip the effect does nothing. Open the [nest](/editing/nests/) and set it on the clips inside.
124	
125	## With an agent
126	
127	An agent sets the effect with `set_audio`'s `voice`: a `kind`, an `amount` from 0 to 1 (1 if left out) and, for `pitch`, `high` and `deep`, a `pitch` from −12 to 12. The kinds are the effects' names in lower case, with `lofi` for Lo-Fi. `{"voice": null}` takes the effect off.
128	
129	Changing the `kind` keeps a stored `pitch` unless the agent sends `pitch: null` with it, where choosing from the list always goes back to the effect's own. An agent can't read Status, though an export still waits for the render. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#voice-effects).
130	
131	## Related
132	
133	- [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
134	- [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/)
135	- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)
136	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)

1	---
2	title: Ducking
3	description: Lower the other clips while this one plays, so music drops under a voice-over and comes back up after it.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Ducking lowers the other clips while this one plays. The usual use is a voice-over: turn ducking on for the voice, and the music drops under it.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking" tools="set_audio" />
12	
13	## Duck the music under a voice-over
14	
15	Set ducking on the clip you want to hear, not on the clip that should get quieter.
16	
17	<Steps>
18	
19	1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
20	
21	2. Open the **Ducking** section and tick **Duck other audio**.
22	
23	3. Set **Level** to how loud the music should be under the voice.
24	
25	</Steps>
26	
27	Ticking the box starts from the defaults: down to 20 %, over 0.5 s, and back up over 1 s. Unticking it, or choosing **Reset** in the section's header, turns ducking off and forgets the settings. The header shows the level, such as "20%", or "off".
28	
29	## The controls
30	
31	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
32	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
33	| **Duck other audio** | Turns ducking on for this clip. | Off | |
34	| **Duck by** | What the ducking follows. See [Choose what it follows](#choose-what-it-follows). | Clip Length | Clip Length, Speech |
35	| **Level** | How loud the other clips are while this one plays. Quick picks: 0, 10, 20, 30 and 50 %. | 20 % | 0–100 % |
36	| **Attack** | How long the other clips take to fall to Level, starting from this clip's first frame. Quick picks: 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
37	| **Release** | How long they take to come back up, starting after this clip ends. Quick picks: 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 s. | 1 s | 0–5 s |
38	| **Pre-roll**, **Hold** | Only for Duck by Speech. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#set-pre-roll-and-hold). | 0.5 s each | 0–5 s |
39	
40	Every control but **Duck other audio** is greyed out until ducking is on. With several clips selected, changing one gives every selected clip all the first clip's ducking settings. See [Edit several clips at once](/audio/sound-tab/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
41	
42	**Level** multiplies whatever the other clips are already doing, so at 20 % a clip at half volume plays at a tenth of its full level. Their own volume, fades and actions still apply underneath.
43	
44	**Attack** and **Release** keep the length you type. They aren't rounded to whole frames. At 0 the level jumps instead of ramping.
45	
46	## Choose what it follows
47	
48	**Duck by** has two choices.
49	
50	**Clip Length** keeps the others down for as long as the clip sits on the timeline, whether or not it's making a sound. They stay lowered through the pauses, so you can see exactly when ducking applies by looking at the timeline, and nothing extra is drawn on the clip.
51	
52	**Speech** lowers them only while this clip's speech plays, so the music comes back up in the pauses. It works only on a clip of a file with sound, and **Duck by** stays greyed out until Frame Job has finished detecting that file's speech. A thin yellow line on the clip shows where the others go down. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
53	
54	## How the level moves
55	
56	The others ramp down from the ducking clip's first frame, hold at Level, and start ramping back up only once the clip has ended. So the music doesn't lift under the last words of a voice-over, and it's still coming back up after the clip has gone.
57	
58	If the Attack is longer than the clip, the others never reach Level, and the release starts from wherever they got to.
59	
60	Each ducked clip's [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) moves with this, so you can see the dip on the clips it lowers.
61	
62	## Good to know
63	
64	- **Overlapping ducking clips multiply.** Two at 50 % give 25 %.
65	- **A silent ducking clip still ducks.** A clip that's muted, silenced by a solo or has its audio switched off still lowers the others. Turn ducking off to stop it. A clip with its audio switched off has no **Sound** sub-tab, so you can't do that there. For the picture half of a [linked pair](/audio/detach-and-attach/), attach the pair first. An agent can use `set_audio`.
66	- **Inside a nest**, a ducking clip lowers the rest of the project over the part of it that plays.
67	- **On a nest clip**, ducking lowers everything for the nest's whole length, and that includes the clips inside the nest. To leave one of them at full level, set ducking on that clip instead, inside the nest.
68	- **The release can miss a clip that follows.** Every clip that overlaps the ducking clip is lowered. A clip that starts after it ends, inside the release, may play at full level. Frame Job can play a clip that follows in the same audio lane as the ducking clip, and a ducking clip never lowers its own lane.
69	- **Ducking can't be animated.** The section is marked ⊘ inside an [action](/audio/animate-sound/), and a change there still applies to the whole clip.
70	
71	## With an agent
72	
73	An agent sets ducking with `set_audio`'s `duck`: a `level` from 0 to 1, an `attack` and a `release`, and a `mode` of `extent` for Clip Length or `speech` for Speech. Its `attack` and `release` can run past the inspector's 5 s. `{"duck": null}` turns ducking off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#ducking).
74	
75	## Related

79	- [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/)

1	---
2	title: Duck by Speech
3	description: Lower the other clips only while this clip's speech plays, so the music comes back up in the pauses.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Duck by Speech lowers the other clips only around this clip's stretches of speech, so the music rises again when the voice stops. It's [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) with **Duck by** set to **Speech**.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by"
13	  tools={['set_audio', 'set_media_speech']}
14	  needs="Nothing. Speech is detected on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Duck only while someone speaks
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
22	
23	2. In the **Ducking** section, tick **Duck other audio**.
24	
25	3. Set **Duck by** to **Speech**.
26	
27	4. Adjust [Pre-roll and Hold](#set-pre-roll-and-hold) if the music moves too early or too late.
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	Level, Attack and Release work as they do for [ducking by clip length](/audio/ducking/#the-controls), but apply to each stretch of speech rather than to the whole clip.
32	
33	## How it follows the speech
34	
35	For each stretch of speech, the attack starts Pre-roll before the first word, the others hold at Level until Hold after the last word, and the release follows.
36	
37	The pauses decide how often the music moves:
38	
39	- A breath under 0.2 s between words doesn't count as a pause.
40	- Stretches whose Pre-roll and Hold meet count as one. At the defaults, that keeps the music down through any pause of 1 s or less.
41	- Where one stretch's release meets the next one's attack, the others follow whichever is lower, so the level never dips below Level.
42	
43	Only the speech in the part of the file the clip plays counts. The stretches follow the clip's speed, reverse and speed ramps.
44	
45	## Set Pre-roll and Hold
46	
47	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
48	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
49	| **Pre-roll** | How long before each stretch of speech the others start going down. Quick picks: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
50	| **Hold** | How long after each stretch of speech the others stay down before the release. Quick picks: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
51	
52	Both are greyed out until **Duck by** is **Speech**, and both keep the length you type, not rounded to whole frames.
53	
54	They can reach past the clip's ends. If the speech starts on the clip's first frame, the others start going down Pre-roll before the clip does. As with [the release](/audio/ducking/#good-to-know), a clip that ends right before this one starts may stay at full level.
55	
56	## Where the speech comes from
57	
58	Frame Job detects speech in every file with sound when it's imported, on your Mac, with the same detection [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses.
59	
60	Choosing **Speech** saves where that file's speech is in the project, in the same undo step. The preview, every export and an agent then all follow the same stretches. A file keeps the speech it was given and isn't detected again, so another clip of the same file uses the same stretches.
61	
62	**Duck by** is greyed out, so you can't choose **Speech**, in two cases:
63	
64	- A selected file's speech is still being detected. Try again in a moment.
65	- A selected clip isn't a clip of a file with sound, such as a nest.
66	
67	Relinking the clip's file to a shorter one keeps the speech that still fits. Relinking it to a file with no sound forgets the speech, and the clip no longer ducks anything.
68	
69	A file with no speech in it ducks nothing.
70	
71	## The line on the timeline
72	
73	A clip that ducks by speech has a thin yellow line across its waveform, so you can see what it's doing to the others. The line is high where they play at full level and low where they're ducked, and it follows the clip's speed, reverse and speed ramps.
74	
75	On a file with no speech the line stays flat along the top. There's no room for it on a very short waveform, and a clip ducking by Clip Length has no line at all. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
76	
77	## Good to know
78	
79	Everything on [Ducking](/audio/ducking/#good-to-know) applies here too. Overlapping ducking clips multiply, a muted clip still ducks, and ducking can't be animated.
80	
81	## With an agent
82	
83	An agent turns on Duck by Speech with `set_audio`'s `duck`, setting `mode` to `speech` with `pre_roll` and `hold` if it wants them, and the file's speech is saved in the same step. It can't do so before the speech is detected, or on a clip that isn't a file with sound. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#ducking).
84	
85	An agent can also do something the inspector can't: give a file stretches of speech of its own with `set_media_speech`, in place of the detected ones, and read them back from `get_project` as `media[].speech`. The times are positions in the file played forward, so they don't change with a clip's speed or direction.
86	
87	It takes up to 100,000 stretches, in order, inside the file's length and not overlapping, though two may touch. Frame Job won't save them for a file with no sound. An empty list says the file has no speech. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/#set_media_speech).
88

1	---
2	title: "Voice Isolation"
3	description: "Keep the voice in a clip and remove background noise and room echo, using Apple's voice model on your Mac."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Voice Isolation keeps the voice in a clip and removes what's around it: background noise and the echo of the room. It uses Apple's on-device voice model, so nothing leaves your Mac.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Isolation"
13	  tools="set_audio"
14	  needs="Nothing. The voice model runs on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Isolate a voice
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Voice Isolation** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
22	
23	2. Tick **Isolate voice**. The Amount goes to 80 % and **Status** reads "Rendering…".
24	
25	3. Keep working. The clip plays without isolation until **Status** reads "Ready", then the editor switches over by itself.
26	
27	4. Listen, and change **Amount** if you need to.
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	Isolation also reduces room echo, so there's no separate control for reverb. The section reminds you with the line "Also reduces room echo" under **Status**.
32	
33	## The controls
34	
35	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
36	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
37	| **Isolate voice** | Turns isolation on at 80 %, or off. | On or off | Off |
38	| **Amount** | How much of the isolated voice replaces the clip's own sound. Quick picks: 50, 80 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
39	| **Status** | What the isolated voice is doing. See [What Status says](#what-status-says). | | Off |
40	
41	Setting **Amount** above 0 also turns isolation on, and 0 turns it off. **Reset** in the section's header does the same as unticking the box.
42	
43	## Choose an amount
44	
45	Amount blends the isolated voice with the clip's own sound.
46	
47	- **At 80 %**, the pauses between words drop by about 14 dB and keep a little of the room, so the voice doesn't sit in dead silence. This is what the box turns on.
48	- **At 100 %**, the pauses are silent.
49	- **Below that**, more of the original sound comes through.
50	
51	Changing Amount takes effect at once. It doesn't need the isolated voice to be worked out again.
52	
53	## While it renders
54	
55	The isolated voice is worked out once for each clip, in the background, when you turn it on. Until it's ready the clip plays without it, and the editor switches over by itself.
56	
57	Trimming or slipping the clip works it out again, because the clip then plays a different part of its file.
58	
59	An export waits for every isolated clip to be ready, and its sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name while it does, so a file is never written without isolation. If a clip's isolated voice can't be made, the export stops with "Clip 12's isolated voice could not be rendered:" and the reason.
60	
61	## What Status says
62	
63	| Status | What it means |
64	| --- | --- |
65	| Off | Isolation is off for this clip. |
66	| Rendering… | The isolated voice is being worked out. The clip plays without it for now. |
67	| Ready | The clip plays with isolation. |
68	| Plays without it at this speed | The clip has a speed change, a ramp or a freeze frame. See below. |
69	| Waits for the reversed copy | The clip is reversed, and its reversed copy isn't ready yet. |
70	| Not rendered: and a reason | It failed. "Not rendered: its media cannot be found" means the clip's file has gone missing, so [relink it](/projects/relink-media/). |
71	| — | Several clips are selected. |
72	
73	## Speed, ramps and freeze frames
74	
75	Isolation plays only at normal speed. A clip with a [speed change](/speed/change-speed/), a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) or a [freeze frame](/speed/freeze-frame/) plays without it, and **Status** says so.
76	
77	A [reversed](/speed/reverse/) clip is isolated once its reversed copy is ready.
78	
79	## Good to know
80	
81	- Isolation comes first in the clip's sound, before the channel choice, the EQ, noise reduction and the compressor. You can use it with [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/), which then works on the isolated sound. A [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) is made from the isolated voice too. See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
82	- Two clips cut from one take are isolated separately, so the sound at the join may differ slightly.
83	- Isolation does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip, and its **Status** reads "Off". Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
84	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Isolate voice** and **Amount** set where the action ends, and the Amount glides across the action, from 0 when the clip's own Amount is 0. The isolated voice is still made for a clip whose own isolation is off.
85	
86	## With an agent
87	
88	`set_audio` sets the amount as `isolation`, from 0 to 1: 0 is off, 0.8 is what the box turns on, and 1 leaves silence between words. An agent can't read **Status**, because the render's state isn't in `get_project`, but an export still waits for it. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#noise-reduction-and-voice-isolation).
89	
90	## Related

93	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
94	- [Voice effects](/audio/voice-effects/)
95	- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)

2	title: "Noise Reduction"
3	description: "Turn down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fans, under speech as well as between words, with no noise sample needed."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Noise Reduction turns down steady background noise such as hiss, hum and fan noise. It works out the noise level from the clip itself, so you don't need to give it a sample of the noise or a stretch of silence.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Noise Reduction" tools="set_audio" />
12	
13	## Remove noise
14	
15	<Steps>
16	
17	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Noise Reduction** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
18	
19	2. Raise **Remove noise** while you listen, until the noise is low enough and the voice still sounds natural.
20	
21	</Steps>
22	
23	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
24	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
25	| **Remove noise** | How much steady background noise to remove. Quick picks: 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 %. | 0 to 100 % | 0 % (off) |
26	| **Depth** | Read-only. See [The Depth readout](#the-depth-readout). | | off |
27	
28	**Reset** in the section's header sets **Remove noise** back to 0.
29	
30	## The Depth readout
31	
32	**Depth** tells you the most any part of the sound can be turned down at this setting. It follows **Remove noise**:
33	
34	| Remove noise | Depth reads |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| 0 % | off |
37	| 25 % | 2 dB at most |
38	| 50 % | 6 dB at most |
39	| 75 % | 12 dB at most |
40	| 100 % | floor removed |
41	
42	Between those it climbs with the setting, so 90 % reads "20 dB at most".
43	
44	Noise Reduction never removes more than the noise level it found, so a higher setting isn't a stronger cut across the whole sound.
45	
46	## What it can't do
47	
48	Noise Reduction isn't a gate. It works under speech as well as between words, and it doesn't silence the gaps. To turn the pauses down, use the [Gate](/audio/gate/).
49	
50	It can't remove a sound that isn't steady, such as a door slam or a cough. A long held note may eventually be treated as noise.
51	
52	To reduce the echo of a room, use [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/). The two work together: Noise Reduction then works on the isolated sound.
53	
54	## Good to know
55	
56	- It runs after the EQ and [hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/), and before the [Gate](/audio/gate/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
57	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, **Remove noise** sets where the action ends and the amount glides across the action.
58	- Noise Reduction set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
59	
60	## With an agent
61	
62	`set_audio` sets the amount as `noise_reduction`, from 0 to 1. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#noise-reduction-and-voice-isolation).
63	
64	## Related

67	- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)
68	- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
69	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)

1	---
2	title: "Hum removal"
3	description: "Notch out mains hum at 50 or 60 Hz and its harmonics, and leave the voice between them alone."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Hum removal cuts the low electrical hum that mains power can leave on a recording. It places a narrow notch at the mains frequency and at each of its multiples, and leaves the sound between the notches alone.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Hum" tools="set_audio" />
12	
13	## Remove hum
14	
15	<Steps>
16	
17	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Hum** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
18	
19	2. Tick **Remove hum**. It starts at 60 Hz, 30 dB deep, with 4 harmonics.
20	
21	3. Set **Mains** to the frequency where the recording was made: 50 Hz in most of the world, 60 Hz in most of the Americas and parts of Asia.
22	
23	4. If you can still hear the hum, raise **Depth** or **Harmonics**.
24	
25	</Steps>
26	
27	The other controls are greyed out until **Remove hum** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns hum removal off.
28	
29	## The controls
30	
31	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
32	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
33	| **Remove hum** | Turns hum removal on. | On or off | Off |
34	| **Mains** | The mains frequency where the recording was made. | 50 Hz or 60 Hz | 60 Hz |
35	| **Depth** | How far each notch turns the hum down. Quick picks: 12, 24, 30 and 48 dB. | 6 to 60 dB | 30 dB |
36	| **Harmonics** | How many notches: the mains frequency and its multiples. Quick picks: 1, 2, 4 and 8. | 1 to 8 | 4 |
37	
38	At 60 Hz with 4 harmonics, the notches sit at 60, 120, 180 and 240 Hz.
39	
40	Each notch is about a tenth of the mains frequency wide, whatever its depth, so a notch at 60 Hz is about 6 Hz wide.
41	
42	## Good to know
43	
44	- Hum removal runs after the [EQ](/audio/eq/). Its notches appear in the EQ section's drawn curve, but the EQ's **Bypass** doesn't turn them off.
45	- Hum removal only reaches the mains frequency and its multiples. For hiss, fans or other steady noise, use [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/), which comes after it.
46	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls set where the action ends. **Depth** glides across the action. **Mains**, **Harmonics** and turning hum removal on or off change at the action's end, with no glide.
47	- Hum removal set on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
48	
49	## With an agent
50	
51	`set_audio` sets the same controls through `hum`, with `frequency`, `depth_db` and `harmonics`. An empty `hum` turns it on at the defaults and `null` turns it off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#hum-removal).
52

1	---
2	title: "Gate"
3	description: "Turn a clip down in the pauses between phrases, so room noise and breaths get quieter while the speech stays as it is."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	The gate turns a clip down in its pauses. When the sound falls below the threshold it's pushed further down, so room noise and breaths between phrases get quieter while the speech itself is untouched. Above the threshold the gate is open and leaves the sound alone. It turns the pauses down, it doesn't cut them out. To take pauses out of the timeline, use [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/).
11	
12	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Gate" tools="set_audio" />
13	
14	<Shot
15	  name="09c-clip-sound-dynamics.inspector"
16	  alt="The Gate section of the Sound tab with Gate pauses ticked: Threshold −10 dB, Ratio 4.0:1, Range 20 dB, Attack 1 ms, Hold 50 ms, Release 100 ms, Status reading Opens above −31.8 dBFS, and Loudness −21.8 LUFS."
17	/>
18	
19	## Gate the pauses
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **Gate** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
24	
25	2. Tick **Gate pauses**. It starts at the [defaults](#the-controls), which work from the clip's own loudness.
26	
27	3. Play the clip. If the ends of words are being cut, raise **Hold** or lower **Threshold**.
28	
29	4. If the pauses aren't quiet enough, raise **Range**. If they sound too empty, lower it.
30	
31	</Steps>
32	
33	The other controls are greyed out until **Gate pauses** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the gate off.
34	
35	## The controls
36	
37	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
38	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
39	| **Threshold** | How far under the clip's loudness the gate opens. | −40 to 0 dB | −10 dB | −20, −15, −10, −6 |
40	| **Ratio** | How strongly sound under the threshold is turned down. At 4:1, each dB under the threshold becomes 3 dB further down. | 1:1 to 20:1 | 4:1 | 2, 4, 10, 20 |
41	| **Range** | The most the gate ever takes away. | 1 to 80 dB | 20 dB | 10, 20, 40, 80 |
42	| **Attack** | How quickly it opens when the sound rises. | 0 to 100 ms | 1 ms | 1, 5, 10 |
43	| **Hold** | How long it stays open after the sound falls, so the ends of words aren't clipped. | 0 to 500 ms | 50 ms | 0, 50, 100, 200 |
44	| **Release** | How quickly it closes after the hold. | 1 to 2,000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 250, 500 |
45	
46	## The threshold follows the clip
47	
48	**Threshold** is set in dB under the clip's own loudness, not at a fixed level, so the same setting works on a quiet recording and a loud one. A trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves the loudness, and the threshold moves with it.
49	
50	That loudness is the Loudness figure in the [Volume](/audio/volume/) section. It's measured before noise reduction, the compressor, the volume, the fades and ducking, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change where the gate opens.
51	
52	## Read Status and Loudness
53	
54	Two readouts at the foot of the section show what the threshold means for this clip. With several clips selected, **Loudness** reads "—". **Status** does too, unless the gate is off on the first of them, when it reads "off".
55	
56	**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−21.8 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.
57	
58	**Status** says where the gate opens, or why it isn't working:
59	
60	| Status | What it means |
61	| --- | --- |
62	| off | **Gate pauses** isn't ticked. |
63	| Opens above −31.8 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. Here, −21.8 LUFS with a −10 dB threshold. |
64	| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. See below. |
65	| Not gating: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
66	| Not gating: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
67	| Not gating: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |
68	
69	## Before the clip's loudness is measured
70	
71	The gate, the [leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [de-esser](/audio/de-esser/) all depend on the clip's measured loudness. Until it's measured, the clip plays without them, and the preview picks them up by itself.
72	
73	An export waits until every gated, levelled or de-essed clip has been measured. After five minutes without a measurement it stops, saying that the clip's loudness or speech hasn't been measured yet, and to wait for the Status rows to show the clip's loudness and export again.
74	
75	A clip that can't be measured, because it's under 0.4 s or too quiet, plays and exports without them, and the export doesn't wait for it.
76	
77	## Good to know
78	
79	- The gate runs after [noise reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) and before the leveller, the de-esser and the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
80	- The gate doesn't look ahead, so a loud start after a long pause can lose its first moment while the gate opens. At the default **Attack**, that's about a millisecond.
81	- There's no way to listen to only what the gate takes away, so judge it by playing the clip.
82	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls set where the action ends. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the gate on or off changes at the action's end.
83	- The gate does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
84	
85	## With an agent
86	
87	`set_audio` sets the same controls through `gate`, with `threshold_db`, `ratio`, `range_db`, `attack`, `hold` and `release`. The three times use an [agent's time units](/mcp/units-and-ids/), not milliseconds. An empty `gate` turns it on at the defaults and `null` turns it off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#gate).
88

1	---
2	title: "De-esser"
3	description: "Tame the hard s, sh and t sounds a close microphone exaggerates, turning down only the top of the voice while they last."
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The de-esser tames sibilance, the hard "s", "sh" and "t" sounds a close microphone exaggerates. It listens to the sound above its frequency and turns only that band down while it's over the threshold, so the rest of the voice keeps its level.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ De-esser" tools="set_audio" />
12	
13	## Reduce sibilance
14	
15	<Steps>
16	
17	1. Select a clip with sound, and open the **De-esser** section of the [Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/).
18	
19	2. Tick **Reduce sibilance**. It starts at 6,000 Hz, a threshold of 0 dB and a range of 6 dB.
20	
21	3. Play a part with hard "s" sounds. If they're still sharp, lower **Threshold** or raise **Range**.
22	
23	4. If the voice sounds dull or lisped, raise **Threshold** or lower **Range**. Move **Frequency** to where the sibilance sits in this voice.
24	
25	</Steps>
26	
27	The other controls are greyed out until **Reduce sibilance** is ticked. **Reset** in the section's header turns the de-esser off.
28	
29	## The controls
30	
31	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
32	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
33	| **Frequency** | Where the sibilant band starts. | 2,000 to 12,000 Hz | 6,000 Hz | 4,000, 5,000, 6,000, 8,000 |
34	| **Threshold** | How loud the band must get, relative to the clip's loudness, before it's turned down. | −30 to +20 dB | 0 dB | −6, −3, 0, 3 |
35	| **Range** | The most the band is turned down. | 1 to 24 dB | 6 dB | 3, 6, 10 |
36	
37	The de-esser never makes any frequency louder. Right at **Frequency** it takes less than half the range, about 2.5 dB of the default 6 dB, and about 5.5 dB an octave above.
38	
39	It reacts in 1 ms and lets go over 60 ms. You can't change those times.
40	
41	## Read Status and Loudness
42	
43	**Threshold** follows the clip's own loudness, the way the [Gate's](/audio/gate/#the-threshold-follows-the-clip) does, so a trim, a pan change or a different channel choice moves it. Two readouts show what it means for this clip. With several clips selected, **Loudness** reads "—". **Status** does too, unless the de-esser is off on the first of them, when it reads "off".
44	
45	**Loudness** is the level the threshold is measured from, for example "−41.7 LUFS". It reads "measuring…" until the clip has been measured.
46	
47	**Status** says where the de-esser acts, or why it isn't working:
48	
49	| Status | What it means |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| off | **Reduce sibilance** isn't ticked. |
52	| Acts above −41.7 dBFS | The clip's loudness plus the **Threshold**. |
53	| Waits for its loudness | The clip hasn't been measured yet. |
54	| Not de-essing: too short | The clip plays for under 0.4 s, too short to measure. |
55	| Not de-essing: too quiet | The clip is too quiet to measure. |
56	| Not de-essing: no sound | The clip plays no sound in this timeline, or it's a nest clip. |
57	
58	Until the clip's loudness is measured it plays without the de-esser, and an export waits. See [Before the clip's loudness is measured](/audio/gate/#before-the-clips-loudness-is-measured).
59	
60	## Good to know
61	
62	- The de-esser runs after the [gate](/audio/gate/) and the [leveller](/audio/leveller/), and before the [compressor](/audio/compressor/). See [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/).
63	- With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, these controls set where the action ends. The numbers glide across the action, and turning the de-esser on or off changes at the action's end.
64	- The de-esser does nothing on a [nest](/editing/nests/) clip. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
65	
66	## With an agent
67	
68	`set_audio` sets the same controls through `de_esser`, with `frequency`, `threshold_db` and `range_db`. An empty `de_esser` turns it on at the defaults and `null` turns it off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#de-esser).
69

72	- [Gate](/audio/gate/)
73	- [EQ](/audio/eq/)
74	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
75	- [Compressor](/audio/compressor/)

1	---
2	title: EQ
3	description: Shape a clip's tone with a high-pass, two shelves, three bands and a low-pass, or start from the Rumble Cut, De-mud and Presence presets.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
9	
10	The EQ turns parts of a clip's sound up or down by frequency. Use it to take out rumble, thin out a boomy voice or make words easier to follow.
11	
12	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ EQ" tools="set_audio" />
13	
14	<Shot
15	  name="09b-clip-sound-eq.inspector"
16	  alt="The EQ section of the Sound sub-tab, reading 2 on, with a Reset button. A response curve falls away below 80 Hz and has four narrow hum notches and a small lift around 4 kHz. Below it are the Bypass checkbox, the Rumble Cut, De-mud and Presence buttons, High-pass ticked at 80 Hz and 24 dB/oct, and Low shelf unticked with its controls greyed out."
17	/>
18	
19	## Shape a clip's tone
20	
21	<Steps>
22	
23	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab. The **EQ** section starts closed, so open it.
24	
25	2. For a voice, press a [preset](#presets). Otherwise tick the [part](#the-seven-parts) you want.
26	
27	3. Set its [Frequency, and its Gain, Q or Slope](#frequency-gain-q-and-slope). The [curve](#the-response-curve) at the top of the section shows the result.
28	
29	4. Tick [**Bypass**](#bypass) to compare with and without.
30	
31	</Steps>
32	
33	The section's header shows how many parts are on, such as "2 on", or "bypassed", or "off". **Reset** appears there once the EQ has settings, and turns the whole EQ off.
34	
35	## Presets
36	
37	Each preset sets one part and turns Bypass off. It leaves the other parts alone, so the three combine.
38	
39	| Preset | What it sets |
40	| --- | --- |
41	| **Rumble Cut** | High-pass on at 80 Hz, 24 dB/oct |
42	| **De-mud** | Band 1 at 300 Hz, −3 dB, Q 1 |
43	| **Presence** | Band 3 at 4 kHz, +3 dB, Q 1 |
44	
45	A preset replaces whatever its part held. Press **De-mud** after setting up Band 1 by hand and your Band 1 settings are gone.
46	
47	## The seven parts
48	
49	The EQ has seven parts, each with its own checkbox, and the sound passes through them in this order. Ticking a part turns it on at its default. Unticking it clears that part's settings and leaves the others as they are, so ticking it again starts from the default. To switch parts off without losing them, use [Bypass](#bypass).
50	
51	A shelf or band starts at 0 dB, and a Gain of 0 dB changes nothing, so you won't hear one until you move its **Gain**. The High-pass and Low-pass take effect as soon as you tick them.
52	
53	### High-pass
54	
55	Turns down everything below its **Frequency**. It starts at 80 Hz and 12 dB/oct, and its quick picks are 40, 60, 80, 100 and 120 Hz.
56	
57	### Low shelf
58	
59	Turns everything below its **Frequency** up or down by its **Gain**. It starts at 100 Hz and 0 dB, and its quick picks are 80, 100, 150 and 200 Hz.
60	
61	### Band 1, 2 and 3
62	
63	Each band turns the frequencies around its **Frequency** up or down by its **Gain**, and **Q** sets how narrow the affected range is. The bands start at 300 Hz, 1000 Hz and 4000 Hz, all at 0 dB and Q 1. All three have the same frequency quick picks: 100, 300, 1000, 2500, 4000 and 8000 Hz.
64	
65	### High shelf
66	
67	Turns everything above its **Frequency** up or down by its **Gain**. It starts at 8000 Hz and 0 dB, and its quick picks are 6000, 8000, 10000 and 12000 Hz.
68	
69	### Low-pass
70	
71	Turns down everything above its **Frequency**. It starts at 12000 Hz and 12 dB/oct, and its quick picks are 8000, 10000, 12000 and 16000 Hz.
72	
73	## Frequency, Gain, Q and Slope
74	
75	A part's controls are greyed out until you tick it. Which ones it has depends on its kind.
76	
77	| Control | What it does | On | Range | Default |
78	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
79	| **Frequency** | Where the part acts: the corner of a pass or shelf, the centre of a band. It's a typed field with quick picks and no slider. | Every part | 20 to 20000 Hz | See [the seven parts](#the-seven-parts) |
80	| **Gain** | How far a shelf or band turns the sound up or down. Quick picks: −6, −3, 0, 3, 6. | Shelves and bands | −24 to +24 dB | 0 dB |
81	| **Q** | How narrow a band is. Higher is narrower. Quick picks: 0.5, 0.7, 1, 2, 4. | Bands | 0.1 to 10 | 1 |
82	| **Slope** | How steeply a pass falls away, in decibels per octave. 24 is the steeper. | High-pass and Low-pass | 12 dB/oct or 24 dB/oct | 12 dB/oct |
83	
84	A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
85	
86	## The response curve
87	
88	The first row of the section draws how much each frequency from 20 Hz to 20 kHz is turned up or down. The middle line is 0 dB. Upright lines mark 100 Hz, 1 kHz and 10 kHz, and level lines mark +12 and −12 dB. The curve covers ±24 dB, and anything past that sits at the edge.
89	
90	The notches from [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/) are drawn on the same curve, so you see the two together.
91	
92	The curve only shows the result. It has no handles to drag. It's greyed while Bypass is on, and it isn't drawn when the selected clips have different EQ or hum settings.
93	
94	## Bypass
95	
96	Tick **Bypass** to silence the EQ and keep its settings, so you can compare with and without. It's off by default, and it's greyed out until the clip has an EQ. Pressing a preset turns it off.
97	
98	## Change the EQ over time
99	
100	With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, the EQ's controls write the action's end. **Frequency**, **Gain** and **Q** move smoothly across the action. **Slope**, **Bypass** and turning a part on or off change at the action's end, with no glide. Unticking a part with an action selected turns it off at the end of the action.
101	
102	**Frequency** has no slider, so when the value at the playhead differs from the one shown, the row says so in words, such as "now 450 Hz".
103	
104	## Good to know
105	
106	- The EQ runs after [Channels](/audio/channels/), and before [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/) and [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/). [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/#the-fixed-signal-order) has the whole order.
107	- The EQ doesn't change the Loudness readout in the Volume section, but [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it.
108	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) presses Rumble Cut for you. [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) with its **EQ** option on replaces the Low shelf, the three bands and the High shelf, keeps the High-pass and Low-pass, and turns Bypass off.
109	- At a cut between two clips, the EQ's settings switch with no glide.
110	- On a nest clip the EQ has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
111	
112	## With an agent
113	
114	`set_audio` sets the same parts through its `eq` argument. A part it leaves out keeps what it holds, `null` turns one part off, and `"eq": null` turns the whole EQ off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#eq).
115	
116	Two things differ from the inspector. Turning a band on at its defaults starts it at 1000 Hz whichever band it is, where the inspector starts the three at 300, 1000 and 4000 Hz. And a value outside its range is an error that changes nothing, where the inspector moves it to the nearest end.
117	
118	To switch one part off at the end of an action, an agent names it in the action's `off` list. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/#switching-off-at-an-end).
119	
120	## Related
121	
122	- [Hum removal](/audio/hum-removal/)
123	- [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/)
124	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)
125	- [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/)
126	- [Animate sound with actions](/audio/animate-sound/)

1	---
2	title: Leveller
3	description: Even out a voice that moves on and off the microphone by bringing each phrase toward a target level, ahead of time.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The leveller evens out a speaker who moves on and off the microphone. It turns each phrase up or down toward a target, working from the whole clip ahead of time, so a phrase starts at its own level and doesn't catch up after it begins. To tame sudden loud moments use the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/), and to bring a whole clip to a delivery loudness use [Normalize](/audio/normalize/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Leveller"
13	  tools="set_audio"
14	  needs="The clip's loudness and its speech, both measured on your Mac with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Ride the level
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab. The **Leveller** section starts closed, so open it.
22	
23	2. Tick **Ride the level**. It turns on at the [defaults](#the-controls).
24	
25	3. Read **Status**. If it says **Aims at** and a level, the clip is being levelled. If it [says anything else](#status-and-loudness-readouts), it's waiting or it can't work on this clip.
26	
27	4. Play the clip, and adjust the controls if a phrase is still too quiet or too loud.
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	The section's header shows the target, such as "0 dB", or "off". **Reset** appears there once the leveller has settings, and turns it off. Unticking **Ride the level** also throws away its settings, so ticking it again starts from the defaults.
32	
33	## How it levels
34	
35	The leveller looks at the clip's speech and splits it into phrases. A pause in the speech of at least half a second ends a phrase, and a shorter gap stays inside it.
36	
37	- **In a phrase**, it measures the level the way a loudness meter does, over about three seconds of speech at a time. It never reaches across a pause into the next phrase.
38	- **In a pause**, it holds the gain it had and doesn't follow the room. In the last quarter of a second of the pause it moves to the next phrase's level.
39	- **A phrase with under a second of speech** takes the level of the last longer phrase before it, or, when there's none, the first one after it. A short "yes" doesn't get a level of its own.
40	
41	## The controls
42	
43	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
44	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
45	| **Target** | Where it aims. | −20 to 10 dB | 0 dB | −6, −3, 0, 3 |
46	| **Max Boost** | The most it turns the clip up. | 0 to 24 dB | 12 dB | 6, 12, 18 |
47	| **Max Cut** | The most it turns the clip down. | 0 to 24 dB | 12 dB | 3, 6, 12 |
48	| **Response** | How smoothly it follows the voice within a phrase. | 0.5 to 10 s | 2 s | 1, 2, 4 s |
49	
50	A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
51	
52	### Target
53	
54	The target is in dB from the clip's own loudness, not an absolute level. At 0 dB each phrase aims at the clip's loudness, and at −3 dB it aims 3 dB under that. Because it follows the clip's loudness, a trim that changes what plays moves the level it aims at.
55	
56	### Max Boost
57	
58	Caps how far a quiet phrase is turned up. Lower it if a faint background voice or a distant mumble is being pulled up too far. At 0 dB the leveller never turns anything up.
59	
60	### Max Cut
61	
62	Caps how far a loud phrase is turned down. At 0 dB the leveller never turns anything down.
63	
64	### Response
65	
66	Changes in a phrase's level shorter than this are smoothed out, before and after alike. A longer Response follows the voice more slowly, and a shorter one follows it more closely.
67	
68	## Status and Loudness readouts
69	
70	**Status** says where the leveller is aiming, what it's waiting for, or why it isn't levelling.
71	
72	| Status says | What it means |
73	| --- | --- |
74	| "Aims at −41.7 LUFS" | It's levelling, toward that level: the clip's loudness plus the Target. |
75	| "Waits for its loudness" | The clip's sound analysis hasn't finished. |
76	| "Waits for its speech" | Speech in the clip hasn't been found yet. |
77	| "Not levelling: it plays no sound in this timeline" | The clip has nothing to measure here. |
78	| "Not levelling: it plays for under 0.4 s" | The clip is too short to measure. |
79	| "Not levelling: it is too quiet to measure" | The clip has no measurable loudness. |
80	| "Not levelling: it has no phrase with 1 s of speech" | No phrase is long enough to measure. |
81	| "Not levelling: speech detection is unavailable" | Speech detection isn't available, and the media has no saved speech. |
82	| "off" | **Ride the level** isn't ticked. |
83	| "—" | Several clips are selected, so select one to read it, or the clip is a nest, where the leveller has no effect. |
84	
85	**Loudness** shows the clip's loudness, which the target is measured from, such as "−41.7 LUFS". LUFS is the unit of loudness. It reads "measuring…" while that's being worked out, and "—" with several clips selected or when there's no reading. It's measured over the part of the clip that plays, before the clip's volume, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change it.
86	
87	## Change the leveller over time
88	
89	With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, the controls write the action's end. **Target**, **Max Boost** and **Max Cut** move smoothly across the action. **Response** changes at the action's end, and so does turning the leveller on or off.
90	
91	## Good to know
92	
93	- The leveller works from the speech found by the clip's sound analysis, or the speech saved for [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
94	- Until the clip's loudness and speech are both measured, it plays without levelling. An export waits for them for up to five minutes, then stops with a message naming the clip. Wait for **Status** to show the clip's loudness and export again.
95	- A clip it can't level, for one of the "Not levelling" reasons above, plays and exports without it.
96	- It works the same in the preview and in an export, from wherever playback starts.
97	- It runs after the [Gate](/audio/gate/) and before the [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/) and the [Compressor](/audio/compressor/), which then get the levelled voice.
98	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it.
99	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) turns the leveller on at its defaults when the speech's loudness varies a lot, and off when it doesn't.
100	- On a nest clip the leveller has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
101	
102	## With an agent
103	
104	`set_audio` sets the same controls through its `leveller` argument. `{}` turns the leveller on at its defaults, and `null` turns it off. A value outside its range is an error that changes nothing. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#leveller).
105

1	---
2	title: Compressor
3	description: Even out a clip's loud and quiet passages by turning down whatever goes above a threshold.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The compressor evens out a clip's loud and quiet passages by turning down whatever goes above a threshold. It reacts moment by moment and acts only on what's over the threshold. For a voice that drifts on and off the microphone, the [Leveller](/audio/leveller/) is the better fit. This page covers a clip's compressor. A track has one of its own, on [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Compressor" tools="set_audio" />
12	
13	## Smooth volume levels
14	
15	<Steps>
16	
17	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab. The **Compressor** section starts closed, so open it.
18	
19	2. Tick **Smooth volume levels**. It turns on at a gentle setting for speech: −18 dB, 3:1, a 10 ms attack and a 200 ms release, with no makeup.
20	
21	3. Play the clip. Lower [**Threshold**](#threshold) until the loud passages come down, and raise [**Ratio**](#ratio) if you want it to act harder.
22	
23	4. Add [**Makeup**](#makeup) to win back the level it took.
24	
25	</Steps>
26	
27	The section's header shows the ratio, such as "3.0:1", or "off". **Reset** appears there once the compressor has settings, and turns it off. Unticking **Smooth volume levels** also throws away its settings, so ticking it again starts from the defaults.
28	
29	## The controls
30	
31	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
32	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
33	| **Threshold** | The level above which it starts turning the sound down. | −60 to 0 dB | −18 dB | −30, −24, −18, −12, −6 |
34	| **Ratio** | How strongly it turns down sound above the threshold. | 1 to 20 :1 | 3:1 | 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 20 |
35	| **Attack** | How quickly it reacts when the level rises. | 0 to 200 ms | 10 ms | 1, 5, 10, 30, 100 ms |
36	| **Release** | How quickly it lets go when the level falls. | 10 to 2000 ms | 200 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 ms |
37	| **Makeup** | Gain added afterwards to make up what the compressor took away. | 0 to 24 dB | 0 dB | 0, 3, 6, 12 |
38	
39	A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
40	
41	### Threshold
42	
43	The threshold is a fixed level, not a distance from the clip's loudness as the [Gate](/audio/gate/)'s is. A quiet recording may never reach the default of −18 dB, and then the compressor does nothing until you lower it.
44	
45	### Ratio
46	
47	At 3:1, sound 3 dB over the threshold comes out 1 dB over it. 1:1 turns nothing down, and 20:1 acts like a limiter.
48	
49	### Attack
50	
51	A short attack catches the start of a word or a sudden peak. A longer one lets those through before the compressor closes in. The time is in milliseconds and isn't rounded to frames.
52	
53	### Release
54	
55	A short release recovers quickly after a loud moment. A longer one lets go more gradually. Like Attack, it isn't rounded to frames.
56	
57	### Makeup
58	
59	Makeup adds a fixed gain after the compressor, so it applies even at 1:1.
60	
61	## Change the compressor over time
62	
63	With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, the controls write the action's end, and each number moves smoothly across the action. Turning the compressor on or off changes at the action's end, with no glide.
64	
65	## Good to know
66	
67	- The compressor acts before the clip's volume, fades and ducking, so moving the Volume slider doesn't change how hard it compresses.
68	- It runs after [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/), the [Gate](/audio/gate/), the [Leveller](/audio/leveller/) and the [De-esser](/audio/de-esser/), so the threshold is compared with sound they've already worked on.
69	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it.
70	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) sets a compressor for you, with its threshold at the speech's typical peak and makeup that gives back the loudness it takes.
71	- On a nest clip the compressor has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
72	
73	## With an agent
74	
75	`set_audio` sets the same controls through its `compressor` argument. `{}` turns the compressor on at its defaults, and `null` turns it off. An agent isn't held to the inspector's Attack and Release ranges, and gives both times in [its own units](/mcp/units-and-ids/). See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#compressor-and-limiter).
76

1	---
2	title: Limiter
3	description: Hold a clip's peaks under a ceiling, so a quiet recording can be turned up without its loudest moments clipping.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	The limiter holds a clip's peaks under a ceiling, so a quiet recording can be turned up without its loudest moments clipping. This page covers a clip's limiter. A track has one of its own, on [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/), and an export has a master limiter, on [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Limiter" tools="set_audio" />
12	
13	## Limit peaks
14	
15	<Steps>
16	
17	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab. The **Limiter** section starts closed, so open it.
18	
19	2. Tick **Limit peaks**. It turns on with a [ceiling](#ceiling) of −1 dBTP and a [release](#release) of 100 ms.
20	
21	3. Turn the clip's volume up as far as you need. The ceiling holds.
22	
23	</Steps>
24	
25	It's a true-peak limiter, which is why its ceiling is in dBTP, decibels of true peak. It looks between the samples, where a peak can sit higher than any sample, and it looks a little ahead, so it turns the sound down smoothly just before a peak and not after it.
26	
27	The section's header shows the ceiling, such as "−1.0 dBTP", or "off". **Reset** appears there once the limiter has settings, and turns it off. Unticking **Limit peaks** also throws away its settings, so ticking it again starts from the defaults.
28	
29	[Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode turns the limiter on for you when a clip needs it, and [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) always does.
30	
31	## Ceiling
32	
33	The highest true peak the clip may reach, from −24 to 0 dBTP. The default is −1 dBTP, and the quick picks are −1, −2, −3 and −6.
34	
35	The ceiling is where the clip's peaks land after its Volume slider, so turning the volume up makes the limiter work harder and doesn't push the clip past the ceiling. Fades and ducking only turn a clip down, so they never take it over either.
36	
37	## Release
38	
39	How quickly the level recovers after a peak, from 1 to 1000 ms. The default is 100 ms, and the quick picks are 50, 100, 200 and 500. The time isn't rounded to frames.
40	
41	A number typed outside either range goes to the nearest end of it.
42	
43	## What it doesn't hold
44	
45	Each clip's limiter holds that clip alone. All of these can go past the ceiling:
46	
47	- Two limited clips that overlap, in a transition or on two tracks.
48	- A clip whose volume an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) raises above its own Volume setting.
49	- A clip inside a nest, when the nest's volume is above 100 %.
50	- A clip on a track whose [volume](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/) is above 0 dB.
51	- The first moments after a hard cut from a louder clip on the same track, while the level settles.
52	
53	In an export, the [master limiter](/export/loudness/#the-master-limiter) holds the whole mix at its own ceiling, whichever of these happens. A [stem](/export/stems/) doesn't go through it. The preview has no master limiter, so they can sound louder while you edit than they do in the file.
54	
55	## Latency compensation
56	
57	Looking ahead delays the sound by 3.3 ms. Frame Job makes up for this on its own: on a track with a limited clip, it starts every clip 3.3 ms early, and the delay brings each one back onto its frame. There's nothing to set.
58	
59	That has two small side effects on such a track. A clip that starts within the first 3.3 ms of the timeline loses up to that much of its start, and the last 3.3 ms of the track aren't heard. [Noise Reduction](/audio/noise-reduction/) has the same effect, with its own delay.
60	
61	## Change the limiter over time
62	
63	With an [action](/audio/animate-sound/) selected, the controls write the action's end. **Ceiling** and **Release** move smoothly across the action, and turning the limiter on or off changes at the action's end, with no glide. A limiter turned on by an action only limits from the action's end, but its [delay](#latency-compensation) applies to the clip's whole track from the start, as one set on the clip itself does.
64	
65	## Good to know
66	
67	- The limiter is last in the clip's chain, after the [**Mix**](/audio/pan-and-mono/) section. [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/#the-fixed-signal-order) has the whole order.
68	- On a nest clip the limiter has no effect. Open the nest with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and set it on the clips inside.
69	
70	## With an agent
71	
72	`set_audio` sets the same controls through its `limiter` argument. `{}` turns the limiter on at its defaults, and `null` turns it off. A value outside its range is an error that changes nothing. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#compressor-and-limiter).
73	
74	## Related

78	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)
79	- [Export loudness](/export/loudness/)

1	---
2	title: Voice effects
3	description: Give a clip's sound one of sixteen effects, from a pitch shift or a phone line to a cathedral, and set how much of it you hear.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Voice Effect changes the character of a clip's sound: pitch a voice up or down, squeeze it into a phone line, or put it in a hall. A clip has one effect at a time.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Voice Effect"
13	  tools="set_audio"
14	  needs="Nothing. Apple's audio units render the effect on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Choose an effect
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
22	
23	2. Open the **Voice Effect** section.
24	
25	3. Choose an effect from **Effect**. The list names each one with its group, such as **Space: Hall**.
26	
27	4. Set [Amount](#set-the-amount), and [Pitch](#set-the-pitch) for the three effects that use it.
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	Frame Job renders the effect in the background, and you hear it [when that's done](#when-you-hear-the-effect). Each effect keeps the clip at about the loudness it had, so switching between them doesn't jump in level.
32	
33	To take the effect off, choose **None**, or choose **Reset** in the section's header. The header shows the effect and its amount, such as "Space: Hall 100%", or "off".
34	
35	With several clips selected, a change applies to all of them. **Amount** and **Pitch** give every selected clip the first clip's whole effect, not only the value you changed. See [Edit several clips at once](/audio/sound-tab/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
36	
37	## The effects
38	
39	The figures here are at an Amount of 100 %.
40	
41	### Voice
42	
43	| Effect | What it does |
44	| --- | --- |
45	| **Voice: Pitch** | Shifts the voice up or down without changing its speed. It starts at 0 semitones, so it changes nothing until you set [Pitch](#set-the-pitch). |
46	| **Voice: High** | Shifts the voice up 5 semitones, cuts the lows below 150 Hz and lifts the highs above 4 kHz by 3 dB, for a small, high voice. |
47	| **Voice: Deep** | Shifts the voice down 5 semitones, adds 4 dB of low weight below 150 Hz and takes 3 dB off the highs above 5 kHz. |
48	| **Voice: Robot** | Makes the voice metallic and buzzing, with a 60 Hz ring modulator and a short 8 ms delay. |
49	
50	### Tone
51	
52	| Effect | What it does |
53	| --- | --- |
54	| **Tone: Bass** | Boosts the lows below 200 Hz by 10 dB. |
55	| **Tone: Treble** | Boosts the highs above 3 kHz by 10 dB. |
56	| **Tone: Bright** | Lifts the presence with 4 dB around 3 kHz, and the air with 6 dB above 8 kHz. |
57	| **Tone: Telephone** | Squeezes the sound into the narrow band of a phone line, 300 Hz to 3.4 kHz. |
58	| **Tone: Radio** | Squeezes the sound into 400 Hz to 4.5 kHz and adds a radio tower's crackle. |
59	
60	### Character
61	
62	| Effect | What it does |
63	| --- | --- |
64	| **Character: Lo-Fi** | Limits the sound to 150 Hz to 6 kHz and crushes it, so it's gritty and dull, like a low-resolution recording. |
65	| **Character: Distorted** | Overdrives the sound into heavy distortion. |
66	
67	### Space
68	
69	| Effect | What it does |
70	| --- | --- |
71	| **Space: Echo** | Repeats the sound every quarter of a second, each repeat darkened above 6 kHz. |
72	| **Space: Room** | Puts the sound in a medium room, with a 35 % reverb mix. |
73	| **Space: Hall** | Puts the sound in a large hall, with a 40 % reverb mix. |
74	| **Space: Plate** | Adds a plate reverb, with a 35 % mix. |
75	| **Space: Cathedral** | Puts the sound in a cathedral with a long tail, with a 45 % reverb mix. |
76	
77	## Set the amount
78	
79	**Amount** is how much of the effect you hear, from 0 to 100 %. It starts at 100 %, and its quick picks are 25, 50 and 100 %. It's greyed out until you choose an effect.
80	
81	Every boost, mix and shift scales with it, and the edges of a band move in from where they'd do nothing. At 50 %, **Voice: High** shifts 2.5 semitones and **Tone: Bass** boosts by 5 dB. At 0 the clip plays as it is.
82	
83	Choosing another effect keeps the Amount. Choosing **None** forgets it, so the next effect starts at 100 %.
84	
85	## Set the pitch
86	
87	**Pitch** is the shift in semitones, from −12 to 12. Its quick picks are −12, −5, 0, 5 and 12. It works only for **Voice: Pitch**, **Voice: High** and **Voice: Deep**, and it's greyed out for the rest.
88	
89	Choosing one of the three sets Pitch back to that effect's own: 0, +5 or −5. Amount scales the shift too, so a Pitch of 12 at an Amount of 50 % shifts by 6 semitones.
90	
91	## Read the status
92	
93	**Status** says where the effect's render has got to. With several clips selected it reads "—".
94	
95	| Status | What it means |
96	| --- | --- |
97	| Off | The clip has no effect, or one that changes nothing, such as an Amount of 0 or **Voice: Pitch** at 0 semitones. |
98	| Rendering… | The effect is being worked out. Until it's done the clip plays without it. |
99	| Ready | The clip plays with the effect. |
100	| Plays without it at this speed | The clip has a speed change, a speed ramp or a freeze frame. An effect plays only at normal speed. |
101	| Waits for the reversed copy | The clip is reversed and its [reversed copy](/speed/reverse/) isn't ready yet. |
102	| Not rendered: and a reason | The render failed. The reason might be "its media cannot be found" or "its isolated voice was not rendered". |
103	
104	## When you hear the effect
105	
106	The effect is worked out once for each clip, in the background. Until it's ready the clip plays without it, and the editor switches over by itself when it is. A clip that isn't at normal speed plays without the effect, and [Status](#read-the-status) says so.
107	
108	Changing the effect, Amount, Pitch or the clip's [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/) amount works it out again. So does trimming or slipping the clip, because the clip then plays a different part of its file. Moving the clip along the timeline doesn't.
109	
110	An export waits for every clip's effect, and its sheet reads "Preparing" and the file's name meanwhile, so a file is never written without one. If a render fails, the export stops and names the clip.
111	
112	## Where it sits in the chain
113	
114	The effect comes right after Voice Isolation and before everything else in the [Sound tab's order](/audio/how-audio-works/). An isolated clip's effect is made from its isolated voice, so it waits for that first. The channel choice, the EQ, noise reduction and the sections after them all work on the effected sound.
115	
116	## Good to know
117	
118	- A reverb or an echo stops at the end of the clip. It doesn't ring on into the next one.
119	- A clip split from a take starts its effect fresh at the cut, so a reverb or echo doesn't carry across the join.
120	- On a stereo file a reverb or an echo mixes the two channels together, so the [channel choice](/audio/channels/) picks from the effected pair, not from the original left and right.
121	- The effect can't be animated. Voice Effect is marked ⊘ inside an [action](/audio/animate-sound/), and a change there still applies to the whole clip. It's also made from the clip's own Voice Isolation amount, not an animated one.
122	- The waveform, the Loudness readout and [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) hear the clip without its effect. [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) in Loudness mode measures through it, and waits for the render first.
123	- On a nest clip the effect does nothing. Open the [nest](/editing/nests/) and set it on the clips inside.
124	
125	## With an agent
126	
127	An agent sets the effect with `set_audio`'s `voice`: a `kind`, an `amount` from 0 to 1 (1 if left out) and, for `pitch`, `high` and `deep`, a `pitch` from −12 to 12. The kinds are the effects' names in lower case, with `lofi` for Lo-Fi. `{"voice": null}` takes the effect off.
128	
129	Changing the `kind` keeps a stored `pitch` unless the agent sends `pitch: null` with it, where choosing from the list always goes back to the effect's own. An agent can't read Status, though an export still waits for the render. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#voice-effects).
130	
131	## Related
132	
133	- [Voice Isolation](/audio/voice-isolation/)
134	- [How audio works](/audio/how-audio-works/)
135	- [The Sound tab](/audio/sound-tab/)
136	- [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/)

1	---
2	title: Ducking
3	description: Lower the other clips while this one plays, so music drops under a voice-over and comes back up after it.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Ducking lowers the other clips while this one plays. The usual use is a voice-over: turn ducking on for the voice, and the music drops under it.
10	
11	<AtAGlance where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking" tools="set_audio" />
12	
13	## Duck the music under a voice-over
14	
15	Set ducking on the clip you want to hear, not on the clip that should get quieter.
16	
17	<Steps>
18	
19	1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
20	
21	2. Open the **Ducking** section and tick **Duck other audio**.
22	
23	3. Set **Level** to how loud the music should be under the voice.
24	
25	</Steps>
26	
27	Ticking the box starts from the defaults: down to 20 %, over 0.5 s, and back up over 1 s. Unticking it, or choosing **Reset** in the section's header, turns ducking off and forgets the settings. The header shows the level, such as "20%", or "off".
28	
29	## The controls
30	
31	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
32	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
33	| **Duck other audio** | Turns ducking on for this clip. | Off | |
34	| **Duck by** | What the ducking follows. See [Choose what it follows](#choose-what-it-follows). | Clip Length | Clip Length, Speech |
35	| **Level** | How loud the other clips are while this one plays. Quick picks: 0, 10, 20, 30 and 50 %. | 20 % | 0–100 % |
36	| **Attack** | How long the other clips take to fall to Level, starting from this clip's first frame. Quick picks: 0.1, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
37	| **Release** | How long they take to come back up, starting after this clip ends. Quick picks: 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 s. | 1 s | 0–5 s |
38	| **Pre-roll**, **Hold** | Only for Duck by Speech. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/#set-pre-roll-and-hold). | 0.5 s each | 0–5 s |
39	
40	Every control but **Duck other audio** is greyed out until ducking is on. With several clips selected, changing one gives every selected clip all the first clip's ducking settings. See [Edit several clips at once](/audio/sound-tab/#edit-several-clips-at-once).
41	
42	**Level** multiplies whatever the other clips are already doing, so at 20 % a clip at half volume plays at a tenth of its full level. Their own volume, fades and actions still apply underneath.
43	
44	**Attack** and **Release** keep the length you type. They aren't rounded to whole frames. At 0 the level jumps instead of ramping.
45	
46	## Choose what it follows
47	
48	**Duck by** has two choices.
49	
50	**Clip Length** keeps the others down for as long as the clip sits on the timeline, whether or not it's making a sound. They stay lowered through the pauses, so you can see exactly when ducking applies by looking at the timeline, and nothing extra is drawn on the clip.
51	
52	**Speech** lowers them only while this clip's speech plays, so the music comes back up in the pauses. It works only on a clip of a file with sound, and **Duck by** stays greyed out until Frame Job has finished detecting that file's speech. A thin yellow line on the clip shows where the others go down. See [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/).
53	
54	## How the level moves
55	
56	The others ramp down from the ducking clip's first frame, hold at Level, and start ramping back up only once the clip has ended. So the music doesn't lift under the last words of a voice-over, and it's still coming back up after the clip has gone.
57	
58	If the Attack is longer than the clip, the others never reach Level, and the release starts from wherever they got to.
59	
60	Each ducked clip's [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) moves with this, so you can see the dip on the clips it lowers.
61	
62	## Good to know
63	
64	- **Overlapping ducking clips multiply.** Two at 50 % give 25 %.
65	- **A silent ducking clip still ducks.** A clip that's muted, silenced by a solo or has its audio switched off still lowers the others. Turn ducking off to stop it. A clip with its audio switched off has no **Sound** sub-tab, so you can't do that there. For the picture half of a [linked pair](/audio/detach-and-attach/), attach the pair first. An agent can use `set_audio`.
66	- **Inside a nest**, a ducking clip lowers the rest of the project over the part of it that plays.
67	- **On a nest clip**, ducking lowers everything for the nest's whole length, and that includes the clips inside the nest. To leave one of them at full level, set ducking on that clip instead, inside the nest.
68	- **The release can miss a clip that follows.** Every clip that overlaps the ducking clip is lowered. A clip that starts after it ends, inside the release, may play at full level. Frame Job can play a clip that follows in the same audio lane as the ducking clip, and a ducking clip never lowers its own lane.
69	- **Ducking can't be animated.** The section is marked ⊘ inside an [action](/audio/animate-sound/), and a change there still applies to the whole clip.
70	
71	## With an agent
72	
73	An agent sets ducking with `set_audio`'s `duck`: a `level` from 0 to 1, an `attack` and a `release`, and a `mode` of `extent` for Clip Length or `speech` for Speech. Its `attack` and `release` can run past the inspector's 5 s. `{"duck": null}` turns ducking off. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#ducking).
74	
75	## Related
76	
77	- [Duck by Speech](/audio/duck-by-speech/)
78	- [Clip volume](/audio/volume/)
79	- [The volume line](/audio/volume-line/)
80	- [Nests](/editing/nests/)
