1	---
2	title: Duck by Speech
3	description: Lower the other clips only while this clip's speech plays, so the music comes back up in the pauses.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Duck by Speech lowers the other clips only around this clip's stretches of speech, so the music rises again when the voice stops. It's [Ducking](/audio/ducking/) with **Duck by** set to **Speech**.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Ducking ▸ Duck by"
13	  tools={['set_audio', 'set_media_speech']}
14	  needs="Nothing. Speech is detected on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Duck only while someone speaks
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the voice clip and open the **Sound** sub-tab of the Clip tab.
22	
23	2. In the **Ducking** section, tick **Duck other audio**.
24	
25	3. Set **Duck by** to **Speech**.
26	
27	4. Adjust [Pre-roll and Hold](#set-pre-roll-and-hold) if the music moves too early or too late.
28	
29	</Steps>
30	
31	Level, Attack and Release work as they do for [ducking by clip length](/audio/ducking/#the-controls), but apply to each stretch of speech rather than to the whole clip.
32	
33	## How it follows the speech
34	
35	For each stretch of speech, the attack starts Pre-roll before the first word, the others hold at Level until Hold after the last word, and the release follows.
36	
37	The pauses decide how often the music moves:
38	
39	- A breath under 0.2 s between words doesn't count as a pause.
40	- Stretches whose Pre-roll and Hold meet count as one. At the defaults, that keeps the music down through any pause of 1 s or less.
41	- Where one stretch's release meets the next one's attack, the others follow whichever is lower, so the level never dips below Level.
42	
43	Only the speech in the part of the file the clip plays counts. The stretches follow the clip's speed, reverse and speed ramps.
44	
45	## Set Pre-roll and Hold
46	
47	| Control | What it does | Default | Range |
48	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
49	| **Pre-roll** | How long before each stretch of speech the others start going down. Quick picks: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
50	| **Hold** | How long after each stretch of speech the others stay down before the release. Quick picks: 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1 s. | 0.5 s | 0–5 s |
51	
52	Both are greyed out until **Duck by** is **Speech**, and both keep the length you type, not rounded to whole frames.
53	
54	They can reach past the clip's ends. If the speech starts on the clip's first frame, the others start going down Pre-roll before the clip does. As with [the release](/audio/ducking/#good-to-know), a clip that ends right before this one starts may stay at full level.
55	
56	## Where the speech comes from
57	
58	Frame Job detects speech in every file with sound when it's imported, on your Mac, with the same detection [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) uses.
59	
60	Choosing **Speech** saves where that file's speech is in the project, in the same undo step. The preview, every export and an agent then all follow the same stretches. A file keeps the speech it was given and isn't detected again, so another clip of the same file uses the same stretches.
61	
62	**Duck by** is greyed out, so you can't choose **Speech**, in two cases:
63	
64	- A selected file's speech is still being detected. Try again in a moment.
65	- A selected clip isn't a clip of a file with sound, such as a nest.
66	
67	Relinking the clip's file to a shorter one keeps the speech that still fits. Relinking it to a file with no sound forgets the speech, and the clip no longer ducks anything.
68	
69	A file with no speech in it ducks nothing.
70	
71	## The line on the timeline
72	
73	A clip that ducks by speech has a thin yellow line across its waveform, so you can see what it's doing to the others. The line is high where they play at full level and low where they're ducked, and it follows the clip's speed, reverse and speed ramps.
74	
75	On a file with no speech the line stays flat along the top. There's no room for it on a very short waveform, and a clip ducking by Clip Length has no line at all. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/).
76	
77	## Good to know
78	
79	Everything on [Ducking](/audio/ducking/#good-to-know) applies here too. Overlapping ducking clips multiply, a muted clip still ducks, and ducking can't be animated.
80	
81	## With an agent
82	
83	An agent turns on Duck by Speech with `set_audio`'s `duck`, setting `mode` to `speech` with `pre_roll` and `hold` if it wants them, and the file's speech is saved in the same step. It can't do so before the speech is detected, or on a clip that isn't a file with sound. See [Tools: clip sound](/mcp/tools-set-audio/#ducking).
84	
85	An agent can also do something the inspector can't: give a file stretches of speech of its own with `set_media_speech`, in place of the detected ones, and read them back from `get_project` as `media[].speech`. The times are positions in the file played forward, so they don't change with a clip's speed or direction.
86	
87	It takes up to 100,000 stretches, in order, inside the file's length and not overlapping, though two may touch. Frame Job won't save them for a file with no sound. An empty list says the file has no speech. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/#set_media_speech).

1	---
2	title: Detach and Attach Audio
3	description: Split a clip's sound onto a linked clip of its own, keep the two in step, and merge them back into one clip.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Detach Audio splits a clip's sound onto its own clip, so you can trim, move or process the sound apart from the picture. Attach Audio merges the two back into one clip.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
12	  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Mix"
14	  tools={['detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'set_enabled']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Detach audio
18	
19	Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** and the **Detach Audio** button in the [Mix section](/audio/pan-and-mono/) of the Sound sub-tab do the same. The menu item is greyed out until something is selected.
20	
21	Each selected clip splits in two, as one undo step named "Detach Audio":
22	
23	- The original clip keeps its picture, and its audio is switched off.
24	- A new clip appears on the track directly below. It plays only sound, from the same file, with the same in point, length and speed, and it keeps the original's audio settings and actions.
25	
26	If the clip is already on the bottom track, Frame Job adds a new track underneath for the sound. Otherwise the sound always goes on the next track down, so make room there first, or drag the sound to another track afterwards.
27	
28	The two clips are now a **linked pair**. Trim the sound on its own to make a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
29	
30	### When Detach Audio won't work
31	
32	Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector:
33	
34	| The reason says | What it means |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| "…media 2 has no audio track" | The clip's file has no sound. |
37	| "…its audio is switched off" | The clip has already been detached, or its sound is otherwise off. |
38	| "…it is not a media clip" | The clip is text, a shape, a graphic, a picture, a freeze frame, a nest or an adjustment clip. |
39	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap by…, more than half of the shorter clip…" | The track below already has a clip where the sound would land. |
40	| "clip 4 would overlap more than one neighbour on one side…" | The sound would reach more than one clip on the track below. |
41	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap, and clip 7 is an adjustment clip…" | The track below has an adjustment clip where the sound would land. |
42	
43	Any other overlap with one clip on the track below, up to half the shorter clip, is allowed and becomes a cross dissolve between the two.
44	
45	With several clips selected, the ones that can be detached are, and the rest are skipped. You only see a reason when none of them could be.
46	
47	## See which clips are linked
48	
49	Each half of a linked pair shows a link symbol after its kind symbol, in the clip's name strip. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because edits to one move both. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/#linked-clips).
50	
51	### A clip with its audio off
52	
53	A clip whose audio is off shows no waveform and no fade handles. A clip with its picture and its sound both off is drawn dimmed. The picture half of a linked pair has no Sound sub-tab, so select the sound half to change anything about the sound. See [Turn a clip's picture or sound off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
54	
55	## What stays in sync
56	
57	A linked picture and sound stay in step in time through your edits.
58	
59	| Edit | What happens to the pair |
60	| --- | --- |
61	| Move | Moving either clip moves both by the same amount. Only the clip you drag changes track, so you can drag the sound to another track and its picture stays where it is. When a move would take either clip past the start of the timeline, both stop together. |
62	| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | A split through both pairs the two halves on each side of the cut. When the cut only crosses one of the clips, the other stays linked to the piece it shares more time with, and the other piece loses its link. |
63	| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Nest](/editing/nests/) and [Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/) | Take both clips. |
64	| [Copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | A selected picture brings its sound, so the pair pastes as a pair. A selected sound is copied on its own, and the pasted copy isn't linked to anything. |
65	| Ripple edits, [Close Gap and Insert Time](/editing/close-gaps/) | Move the other half too. |
66	| [Trim and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone) | On the picture, the edit carries to the sound when their edges line up. On the sound, it moves the sound alone. |
67	| [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) | Slips both, as far as the one with less room allows. |
68	| Delete | Deleting the picture deletes its sound too. See [Remove a clip's sound](#remove-a-clips-sound). |
69	| [Speed](/speed/change-speed/) and [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) | Frame Job won't do these on a linked clip. See [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed). |
70	
71	A ripple edit that would push a sound starting before its picture past the start of the timeline doesn't happen at all. The reason at the foot of the inspector says the sound "would start before 0".
72	
73	Locks win over links. A partner on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) isn't moved, split, trimmed, slipped, duplicated, nested or deleted with its clip. **Copy** is the exception: a selected picture brings its sound even from a locked track.
74	
75	## Remove a clip's sound
76	
77	To drop a clip's sound for good, detach it, select the sound half and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. The picture stays, silent, and its link is gone.
78	
79	Undo brings the sound back. Once the sound clip is gone, no control in the app turns the picture's own audio back on.
80	
81	## Attach audio
82	
83	Select either half of a pair and press <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Attach Audio**. The **Attach Audio** button in the Mix section does the same, but it's only there with the sound half selected, because the picture half has no Sound sub-tab.
84	
85	The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip is removed. Its track stays, empty if nothing else is on it. With several pairs selected, each one merges, as one undo step named "Attach Audio".
86	
87	**Clip ▸ Attach Audio** is greyed out until the selection holds a linked clip. The button stays live, and beeps if the selection holds none.
88	
89	### When Attach Audio won't work
90	
91	The two halves have to match, because they're becoming one clip. They need the same start, length, in point and speed, and the same actions at the same times with the same curves. Otherwise the reason at the foot of the inspector says "clip 4's picture and clip 5's sound do not cover the same time; trim them to match before Attach Audio". This is what a J-cut or an L-cut does on purpose. Trim the two to the same start and end first, and remove or match any action you added to only one half.
92	
93	## Actions and speed
94	
95	The new sound clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/#detach-audio).
96	
97	A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) keeps it: the sound clip's copy of the Speed actions gives it the same ramp, so the two stay in step.
98	
99	Frame Job won't change the speed or direction of either half while they're linked, because the two would have to be re-timed identically. That covers Speed, Reverse, rate stretch, [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/), and adding, moving, changing or removing a Speed action. The reason at the foot of the inspector says "clip 4 is linked to clip 5: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". During a drag, such as a rate stretch, nothing moves and no reason appears. Attach, make the change, then detach again.
100	
101	Attaching keeps the sound's work. The picture takes the sound clip's audio settings, and each of its actions takes the audio values of the sound clip's action at the same place.
102	
103	## With an agent
104	
105	[`detach_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#detach_audio) and [`attach_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#attach_audio) do what the **Clip** menu does, for the one clip you name in `clip`. For `attach_audio`, either half will do.
106	
107	`set_enabled` turns a clip's picture or sound on or off directly, which no control in the app does. After a detached sound has been deleted, it's the way to switch the picture's own audio back on. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#set_enabled).
108

1	---
2	title: J-cuts and L-cuts
3	description: Let a shot's sound start before its picture, or run on under the next shot, by trimming the sound half of a linked pair.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A J-cut brings in the next shot's sound before its picture. An L-cut lets a shot's sound run on under the next shot. Both soften a cut, and in Frame Job both come from trimming the sound half of a [detached clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  keys={['W', 'E']}
13	  where={["Timeline: drag a detached sound clip's edge", 'Timeline: ⌥⇧-drag an edge to roll']}
14	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Make a J-cut
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the later shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> to [detach its audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/#detach-audio).
22	
23	2. If the shot before it is detached too, drag this sound to a track of its own. See [Keep the sound off its neighbour](#keep-the-sound-off-its-neighbour).
24	
25	3. Drag the sound clip's start edge to the left.
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	The sound now begins before its picture. The picture stays where it is.
30	
31	## Make an L-cut
32	
33	<Steps>
34	
35	1. Select the earlier shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>.
36	
37	2. If the next shot's sound is on the track the sound went to, drag this sound to a track of its own.
38	
39	3. Drag the sound clip's end edge to the right.
40	
41	</Steps>
42	
43	The sound now runs on after its picture has ended.
44	
45	## Keep the sound off its neighbour
46	
47	When two neighbouring shots are both detached, their sounds sit side by side on one track. Lengthening one into the other overlaps them, and an overlap on a track is a [cross dissolve](/audio/crossfades/), not a split edit. On a track of its own, the sound overlaps nothing.
48	
49	## How far the sound can go
50	
51	A trim can only reveal what's in the file. The sound stops at the first or last frame of its media, and at the start of the timeline. Choose a shot with spare sound before its in point for a J-cut, or after its out point for an L-cut.
52	
53	The sound has to keep at least one frame. If it runs into another clip on its track, Frame Job allows an overlap of up to half the shorter clip and won't go further.
54	
55	## Trim and roll a sound clip alone
56	
57	The half you grab decides what moves. An edit on the sound moves only the sound. An edit on the picture also moves the sound when their edges line up. A lead you've already made isn't lined up, so trimming that picture's start leaves the sound alone.
58	
59	Dragging is what lengthens a sound. <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> [trim to the playhead](/editing/trimming/#trim-to-the-playhead), so they only shorten it, and they do it to the sound alone. To roll the cut between two sound clips on one track, hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the edge between them. A sound on a track of its own has no cut to roll.
60	
61	See [Move a sound clip's edge alone](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone).
62	
63	## Good to know
64	
65	- Moving either half keeps the lead. When a drag would take the sound past the start of the timeline, both clips stop together.
66	- A ripple edit that would push a leading sound past the start of the timeline doesn't happen.
67	- Frame Job won't [attach](/audio/detach-and-attach/#attach-audio) a pair that no longer covers the same time. Trim the two to the same start and end first.
68	- [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) takes both halves, unless the other half is on a locked track.
69	
70	## With an agent
71	
72	In the app, a trim on a sound moves it alone. An agent has to ask for that: pass `alone: true` to `trim_start`, `trim_end` or `roll` on the sound. Without it, a trim on a sound whose edge lines up with its picture moves both. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start).
73

1	---
2	title: Mute and solo tracks
3	description: Silence a track, or hear only the tracks you pick, and see what that does to the picture, nests and an export.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Mute silences one track. Solo silences every other track, so you can hear one part of the mix by itself. Neither touches the picture.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Track ▸ Mute Audio', 'Track ▸ Solo']}
12	  where={['The speaker and headphones switches in the track header', "The track's right-click menu"]}
13	  tools="set_track"
14	/>
15	
16	## Mute a track
17	
18	Click the speaker switch in the track's header. Every clip on the track goes silent, and the picture is unaffected. Click it again to bring the sound back.
19	
20	**Mute Audio** in the track's right-click menu does the same for the track you clicked. **Track ▸ Mute Audio** acts on the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track): the track of the first selected clip, or the front track when nothing is selected.
21	
22	To silence one clip and not its whole track, use its own [**Mute**](/audio/volume/#mute-a-clip).
23	
24	## Solo a track
25	
26	Click the headphones switch in the track's header, or choose **Solo** in the track's right-click menu or the **Track** menu. The tracks beside it go silent: the other timeline tracks or, inside a nest, that nest's other tracks.
27	
28	You can solo several tracks. All the soloed tracks play, and the rest are silenced.
29	
30	**Solo** shows a checkmark in the **Track** menu while it's on. Neither **Solo** nor **Mute Audio** has a keyboard shortcut. Each click is one undo step, named "Mute Track" or "Solo Track".
31	
32	## How mute and solo combine
33	
34	- **Mute always wins.** A track that's both muted and soloed stays silent.
35	- **Solo doesn't look at what's on the track.** A soloed track with nothing on it still silences the rest, as a mixer's solo button does.
36	- **Pictures stay.** A silenced track still draws. To take a picture out, use [Hide Video](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#hide-video), which leaves the sound playing.
37	
38	## See what a solo silences
39	
40	Under a solo, the waveforms on silenced tracks draw faded, as they do on a muted track. Their speaker switches stay unlit, because a speaker shows that track's own setting and not what a solo is doing to it. So the waveform tells you what you'll hear, and the switch tells you what you've set.
41	
42	## Mute and solo in nests
43	
44	A solo only reaches the tracks beside it:
45	
46	- A solo on a timeline track silences the other timeline tracks, and a nest playing on one of them goes silent with it.
47	- A solo on a track inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) affects only that nest's other tracks.
48	
49	Muting the track a nest clip sits on silences everything inside the nest. A new nest's tracks copy the mute and solo of the tracks they came from, so a muted track's clips stay silent once they're nested. Un-nesting doesn't keep what's set on the nest's tracks.
50	
51	## In an export
52	
53	Mute and solo are part of the project, so the export hears what you hear. A silenced track isn't in the exported mix, and it writes no [stem](/export/stems/). If every track is silenced, Frame Job won't write stems.
54	
55	:::caution
56	A solo left on silences the rest of the export. Check the header switches before you export.
57	:::
58	
59	## Good to know
60	
61	- The switches are plain toggles. <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking one does what a click does, and <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking the header away from its switches [selects the track's clips](/timeline/tracks/#the-track-header).
62	- A [scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/) plays the same mix, so mute and solo silence it too.
63	- The header's other switches are on [The track header](/timeline/tracks/#the-track-header).
64	
65	## With an agent
66	
67	`set_track` sets the same switches. Name the `track` and pass `muted` or `solo` as true or false. It's a direct setting, not a toggle, so asking for what's already set changes nothing. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
68

73	- [Hide and lock tracks](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/)

1	---
2	title: Track volume and pan
3	description: Set a whole track's level and left-right balance in the Track Mix panel, on top of what each clip already does.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Each track has its own volume and pan, applied on top of every clip on it. Use them to balance a music bed against a voice-over without touching each clip.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
12	  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
13	  tools="set_track"
14	/>
15	
16	## Open the Track Mix panel
17	
18	Click the sliders switch, the fifth in the track's header. **Mix…** in the track's right-click menu does the same. **Track ▸ Mix…** opens it for the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track), and has no keyboard shortcut.
19	
20	A small panel opens beside the header, with the track's name at the top. It holds **Volume**, **Pan**, the track's [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/), and **Reset**.
21	
22	There's one panel per timeline, so opening it on another track closes the first. Clicking away closes it, and so does anything that takes its track away: removing the track, undoing it away, or going into or out of a nest.
23	
24	The sliders switch is lit while the track's volume or pan is off its default, or a compressor or limiter is on.
25	
26	## Set a track's volume
27	
28	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
29	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
30	| **Volume** | The track's level, as a slider and a field in dB. Beside them, a readout shows the level as a percentage, or "Off". | Off (at −60) to +12 dB | 0 dB |
31	
32	The quick picks on the field are −12, −6, −3, 0, +3 and +6 dB. Drag the slider to its left end, or type −60, to turn the track off. A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
33	
34	Track volume multiplies what's on the track. A clip at 200 % on a track at −12 dB plays at −6 dB. A muted track is silent whatever its volume.
35	
36	## Set a track's pan
37	
38	| Control | What it does | Range | Default |
39	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
40	| **Pan** | Leans the track's sound left or right, as a slider and a field. | −100 (left) to 100 (right) | 0 |
41	
42	The quick picks are −100, −50, 0, 50 and 100.
43	
44	Pan is a balance, like a [clip's pan](/audio/pan-and-mono/), and keeps the overall loudness steady as it moves. It applies after each clip's own pan, and two pans multiply, so a clip panned left on a track panned left leans further left. It has no effect on a mono source.
45	
46	## Reset the mix
47	
48	**Reset** puts the volume back to 0 dB and the pan to the centre, and turns the track's compressor and limiter off. Inside an open nest, it resets volume and pan only. It's greyed out when there's nothing to reset.
49	
50	Each change is one undo step. A drag, a typed value or a quick pick is named "Track Volume" or "Track Pan", and **Reset** is named "Reset Track Mix".
51	
52	## Track volume in a nest
53	
54	A clip inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) plays through its own track inside the nest, and through the track the nest clip sits on.
55	
56	- **Nesting from one track keeps its sound.** The nest's copy of that track starts at 0 dB and centre, because the track the nest clip lands on still applies.
57	- **Clips from the selection's other tracks** keep their own track's volume and pan inside the nest, and also get the destination track's.
58	- **Un-nesting** puts the clips back on the timeline's tracks without the nest's track settings.
59	- **Mix to mono on a nest clip** folds everything inside it, so the pans of the tracks inside no longer apply.
60	
61	## What hears track volume
62	
63	Track volume is part of what you hear, so it shows up wherever Frame Job measures the mix, and not where it measures a clip.
64	
65	| Hears it | Doesn't hear it |
66	| --- | --- |
67	| The preview and every export, which sound the same | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
68	| The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) | The [Loudness readout](/audio/volume/#read-the-level) |
69	| [Remove Silences](/cleanup/remove-silences/) | A clip's [limiter](/audio/limiter/) |
70	
71	So a track turned up can take a limited clip past its ceiling. Use the track's own [limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) to hold what the whole track hands the mix.
72	
73	## Good to know
74	
75	A track's volume and pan are one value for the whole track, and can't change over time. To ride the level, use a clip's [volume line](/audio/volume-line/) or [actions](/audio/animate-sound/).
76	
77	## With an agent
78	
79	`set_track` sets both, with different scales from the panel. `volume` is a linear gain from 0 to 4, where 1 is 0 dB, 4 is +12 dB and 0 is silent. `pan` runs from −1 (left) to 1 (right). A value outside those ranges changes nothing, where a number typed in the panel goes to the nearest end. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
80

1	---
2	title: Track compressor and limiter
3	description: Compress and limit a track's whole sound, or everything in a nest together, and know where the preview differs from the export.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A track can have its own compressor and limiter, acting on the sound of every clip on it together. Use them to even out a whole voice-over, or to hold a music bed under a ceiling, without setting each clip. This page covers a track's. A clip has its own [compressor](/audio/compressor/) and [limiter](/audio/limiter/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Track ▸ Mix…"
13	  where={['The sliders switch in the track header', "Mix… in the track's right-click menu"]}
14	  tools="set_track"
15	/>
16	
17	## Turn on a track's compressor or limiter
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Open the [Track Mix panel](/audio/track-volume-and-pan/#open-the-track-mix-panel) for the track.
22	
23	2. Tick **Compressor** or **Limit peaks**, below **Pan**. Each turns on at its defaults, and its rows stop being greyed out.
24	
25	3. Adjust the rows.
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	Unticking throws the settings away, so ticking again starts from the defaults. **Reset** at the foot of the panel turns both off, and resets the track's volume and pan too.
30	
31	The header's sliders switch stays lit while either is on.
32	
33	## Where they sit
34	
35	Both act on the track's whole sound: every clip on it, after each clip's own processing, its volume, fades, crossfades and ducking, and after the track's volume and pan. The compressor runs first, then the limiter.
36	
37	A track's compressor and limiter hear the track after its fader. That's the difference from a clip's compressor, which hears the clip before its volume. Turning the track down turns down what reaches them, so a compressor at −20 dB over a track at −6 dB compresses less.
38	
39	## Compressor settings
40	
41	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
42	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
43	| **Compressor** | Turns the track's compressor on. | on, off | off | |
44	| **Threshold** | The level above which it starts turning the track down. | −60 to 0 dB | −18 dB | −30, −24, −18, −12, −6 |
45	| **Ratio** | How strongly it turns down sound above the threshold. | 1 to 20 :1 | 3:1 | 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 8, 20 |
46	| **Attack** | How quickly it reacts. | 0 to 200 ms | 10 ms | 1, 5, 10, 30, 100 ms |
47	| **Release** | How quickly it lets go. | 10 to 2000 ms | 200 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 ms |
48	| **Makeup** | Gain added afterwards. | 0 to 24 dB | 0 dB | 0, 3, 6, 12 |
49	
50	## Limiter settings
51	
52	| Control | What it does | Range | Default | Quick picks |
53	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
54	| **Limit peaks** | Turns the track's limiter on. | on, off | off | |
55	| **Ceiling** | The highest true peak the track may hand the mix. | −24 to 0 dBTP | −1 dBTP | −1, −2, −3, −6 |
56	| **Release** | How quickly the level recovers after a peak. | 1 to 1000 ms | 100 ms | 50, 100, 200, 500 ms |
57	
58	Each control is a slider and a field. A number typed outside the range goes to the nearest end of it.
59	
60	## Use a track as a nest's bus
61	
62	A bus is one path that several sounds share. A [nest's](/editing/nests/) whole mix plays through the track its nest clip sits on, so a compressor or limiter on that track acts on everything inside the nest together. Put a voice's clips in a nest and compress them as one, whatever tracks they're on inside it.
63	
64	A nest's own tracks have no compressor or limiter. Inside an open nest, both sections are greyed out, and their tooltip says "A nest's mix plays through the dynamics of the track that holds it." **Volume**, **Pan** and **Reset** still work there.
65	
66	Nesting a selection doesn't copy a compressor or limiter from the tracks it came from. The track the nest clip lands on keeps its own.
67	
68	## Exact in the export, approximate in the preview
69	
70	An export plays each track with a compressor or limiter through them on its own, before the tracks are mixed. That's exact, and a [stem](/export/stems/) of that track includes them. The [master limiter](/export/loudness/) still runs over the mix afterwards.
71	
72	The preview can only approximate this. Where a track's clips overlap, such as a crossfade or a nest's tracks, the preview plays the track's sound in more than one piece and runs the compressor and limiter on each piece separately. So the pieces can add up past a track limiter's ceiling while you edit, even though the export holds it.
73	
74	While any track has a compressor or limiter and the preview plays at normal speed, the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/) says so in its footer: "The mix as the preview plays it, with track compressors and limiters approximate, before the export's loudness and master limiter."
75	
76	:::tip
77	Judge a track limiter's ceiling on the export, not on the preview's meters.
78	:::
79	
80	## What hears them
81	
82	| Hears them | Doesn't hear them |
83	| --- | --- |
84	| The preview, approximately | [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) |
85	| The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) and the [Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/), approximately | The [Loudness readout](/audio/volume/#read-the-level) |
86	| Every export and stem, exactly | [Enhance Voice](/audio/enhance-voice/) and [Match Audio](/audio/match-audio/) |
87	| | A [scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/) |
88	
89	Normalize, the Loudness readout, Enhance Voice and Match Audio work on the clip itself, before the track.
90	
91	## Good to know
92	
93	- A track's compressor and limiter are one setting for the whole track, and can't change over time. A track has no EQ or other effects.
94	- Each change is one undo step. Turning one on or off, a drag or a typed value is named "Track Compressor" or "Track Limiter", and **Reset** is named "Reset Track Mix".
95	- A track with a limiter plays 3.3 ms later in the preview, and Frame Job places it 3.3 ms earlier to match, so it stays in sync.
96	
97	## With an agent
98	
99	`set_track` sets both, through its `compressor` and `limiter` arguments. Each takes the whole setting at once, so any value you leave out goes to its default, and `null` turns it off. As in the panel, a nest's own tracks can't have them. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#a-tracks-compressor-and-limiter).
100

2	title: Hear a scrub
3	description: Hear the sound under the playhead as you click or drag along the timeline ruler, to find a word or a beat.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	When you click or drag along the ruler, you hear the sound under the playhead. Use it to find a word or a beat by ear.
9	
10	<AtAGlance where="Click or drag along the timeline ruler" />
11	
12	## Scrub the sound
13	
14	Drag along the [ruler](/timeline/ruler-and-playhead/). Playback pauses first if it was running. As the playhead reaches new frames, Frame Job plays about 80 ms of the mix forward from it, with a 5 ms fade at each end so the pieces don't click. A fast drag skips frames, because each new piece waits until the last one has almost played.
15	
16	- A click on the ruler plays one piece.
17	- Hold the mouse still and the sound stops within about a tenth of a second.
18	- Let go and it stops.
19	
20	Dragging left plays each piece forwards from the playhead, not backwards, so a word stays recognisable.
21	
22	## What you hear
23	
24	A scrub plays the mix you'd hear in playback: each clip's volume, fades, ducking, pan and mono, each track's volume and pan, mute and solo, and each clip's sound processing.
25	
26	Three things differ from playback:
27	
28	- A clip's sound processing, such as its compressor or noise reduction, starts fresh in each piece, so it can sound different from a steady play.
29	- A track's [compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/) aren't in a scrub.
30	- The [level meter](/audio/level-meter/) stays still.
31	
32	## Silence a scrub
33	
34	Scrub audio is always on, with no setting, no key and no agent tool. To silence it, [mute or solo](/audio/mute-and-solo/) tracks, or turn down your Mac's volume.
35	
36	## Good to know
37	
38	- Only a scrub on the ruler is heard. Stepping with <kbd>←</kbd> and <kbd>→</kbd>, **Go** in the [Markers list](/timeline/markers/#the-markers-list), and an agent moving the playhead are all silent.
39	- A scrub doesn't use the microphone, so it never asks for that permission.

1	---
2	title: "The level meter"
3	description: Read the two-row meter in the timeline bar to see how loud the mix is while it plays, and whether it reaches full scale.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	The level meter shows how high the mix you're hearing sits while the timeline plays, and warns you when a sample reaches full scale, the loudest level digital sound can hold.
9	
10	<AtAGlance where="The timeline bar, left of the zoom controls" />
11	
12	## What it shows
13	
14	The meter shows what you hear: each clip's volume, fades, ducking, mute and solo, and the compressor and other effects. Press play and it moves. There's nothing to turn on.
15	
16	It has two rows, one per channel, with the left channel on top. A mono track shows in both rows, and a track with more than two channels shows only its first two.
17	
18	At normal speed it measures the mix itself, so two tracks playing the same sound read as one louder sound, and a sound and its inverse read as silence. At any other speed it adds up each track's level instead. That can read a little higher than the mix, and it can light the clip cell when the mix itself wouldn't reach full scale.
19	
20	## Read the meter
21	
22	Each row runs from −60 dB on the left to 0 dB on the right. The scale is even in dB, so the middle of a row is −30 dB. It has no tick marks.
23	
24	| Part | What it tells you |
25	| --- | --- |
26	| **Solid bar** | The average (RMS) level. It rises at once and falls at 24 dB a second. |
27	| **Lighter wash** behind the bar | The instantaneous peak. It rises and falls the same way, and it's never shorter than the bar. |
28	| **Peak-hold mark** | The highest recent level. It stays for about 1.2 seconds, then falls at 12 dB a second. |
29	| **Clip cell** at the right end of each row | Lights for 2 seconds whenever a sample in that row reaches full scale. |
30	
31	A level above 0 dB fills the row and goes no further, so the clip cell is what tells you the mix went over.
32	
33	## When playback stops
34	
35	The bars fall back to the floor. The peak-hold mark stops waiting and falls with them, and a lit clip cell stays lit for the rest of its 2 seconds. The whole meter is at rest within about 3 seconds.
36	
37	## Good to know
38	
39	- The meter shows peaks and average level, not loudness. For LUFS and true peak, use [the Loudness Meter](/audio/loudness-meter/).
40	- It shows the preview's mix. An export also goes through a master limiter, so what an export measures can differ. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
41	- There's one meter for the whole app. With two projects open, the meter in both windows follows the one that's playing, and stopping one project doesn't blank the meter while the other plays on.
42	- In a narrow window the meter gets smaller, and below 40 points wide it isn't drawn at all.
43	- The recorder panel has its own meter for the microphone. See [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/).
44	
45	## Related

1	---
2	title: "The Loudness Meter"
3	description: Show a live column beside the preview that measures your mix in LUFS and true peak while it plays at normal speed.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';
8	
9	The Loudness Meter tells you how loud your mix really is, measured the way the loudness standards EBU R 128 and ITU-R BS.1770 measure it, while the preview plays at normal speed.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="View ▸ Loudness Meter"
13	  keys="⌃⌘L"
14	  where="A column at the right of the preview, left of the scopes"
15	/>
16	
17	<Shot
18	  name="04c-editor-loudness.preview"
19	  alt="The preview with the Loudness column at its right edge, before anything has played. The column has a Reset arrow at the top, M and S bars on a scale from 0 to −48 with a thin blue line across them just above −18, then Momentary, Short-term, Integrated and True peak max, each reading a dash, and a note saying this is the mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness and master limiter."
20	/>
21	
22	## Show the meter
23	
24	Choose **View ▸ Loudness Meter** or press <kbd>⌃⌘L</kbd>. The same command hides it, and the menu item has a tick while the column is showing. The column is 132 points wide and as tall as the preview pane, and the picture makes room for it. The command is always available.
25	
26	Then play the timeline at normal speed. The figures start at "—" and fill in as Frame Job measures.
27	
28	To measure a whole timeline, start at the beginning and play it through without jumping. **Integrated** is then the loudness of everything that played.
29	
30	## What it measures
31	
32	The meter measures the mix you hear, at the level you hear it. It only reads what plays, so it never changes the project or an export.
33	
34	Measuring carries on while the column is hidden. If you show it partway through a pass, the figures already include what has played.
35	
36	A mono track counts in both channels. A track with more than two channels counts by its first two.
37	
38	## The four figures
39	
40	| Figure | What it measures |
41	| --- | --- |
42	| **Momentary** | The last 0.4 seconds. |
43	| **Short-term** | The last 3 seconds. |
44	| **Integrated** | Everything measured since the last reset, with quiet passages left out as the standard says. |
45	| **True peak max** | The highest true peak since the last reset. It turns coral above −1 dBTP. |
46	
47	Figures have one decimal place, such as `−18.4 LUFS` or `−0.6 dBTP`. LUFS is the standard unit of loudness, and a step of 1 LU on its scale is 1 dB. A true peak is the highest point the sound reaches, including between samples, and dBTP is its level in decibels.
48	
49	| You see | It means |
50	| --- | --- |
51	| "—" | There's no figure yet. Momentary needs 0.4 seconds of measuring and Short-term needs 3. Integrated stays at "—" until something loud enough to count has played, so it stays there through digital silence. |
52	| "−∞" | Digital silence. |
53	
54	## The M and S bars
55	
56	The two bars show Momentary (**M**) and Short-term (**S**) on a scale from −48 to 0 LUFS, with a tick every 6 LU. A bar is empty while its figure is "—", and during digital silence.
57	
58	## The target line
59	
60	A thin line in the accent colour crosses both bars at the target in the [Normalize](/audio/normalize/) row, which is −16 LUFS unless you've changed it. It shows you where the mix sits against the level Normalize aims for.
61	
62	The line moves as soon as you change the target, even while the preview is paused. The target can go as low as −50 LUFS, and anything below −48 draws at the bottom of the scale. The line stays at the stored target when Normalize is in Peak mode.
63	
64	## Start measuring again
65	
66	Click the **Reset** button, the ↺ at the top of the column. All four figures go back to "—" and the next sound starts a new measurement.
67	
68	The meter also starts again by itself when you jump somewhere else, such as a seek, the loop going round, or playing from another place. It does the same if Frame Job can't keep up with the audio, because a measurement with a hole in it would be wrong.
69	
70	These don't restart it:
71	
72	- Pausing and playing on. Nothing is counted twice.
73	- An edit.
74	- A gap between clips.
75	- Holding a menu open.
76	- Stepping back by less than a second.
77	
78	When playback stops, the figures stay where they were.
79	
80	## Measuring only at normal speed
81	
82	The meter measures at ×1 only. At any other speed, such as while you [shuttle](/timeline/playback/):
83	
84	- Momentary and Short-term show "—" and their bars go empty.
85	- The note reads "Measured only at normal speed."
86	- Integrated and True peak max keep their values.
87	
88	When you stop, Momentary and Short-term go back to their last normal-speed values.
89	
90	## The note under the figures
91	
92	The note says what's being measured, and when to take the figures with care.
93	
94	| The note says | When |
95	| --- | --- |
96	| "The mix as the preview plays it, before the export's loudness and master limiter." | Usually. |
97	| "The mix as the preview plays it, with track compressors and limiters approximate, before the export's loudness and master limiter." | While any track has a [compressor or limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/). They're approximate in the preview and exact in an export. |
98	| "Measured only at normal speed." | While playing at any other speed. |
99	
100	An export with a loudness target changes the level after this point, and the master limiter holds its peaks under the ceiling, so the export's own report can differ from what you see here. See [Export loudness](/export/loudness/).
101	
102	## Good to know
103	
104	- The meter belongs to its window. A new window starts with the column off and the meter empty.
105	- Nothing is saved. Closing the window ends the measurement, and the column is off the next time you open the project.
106	
107	## With an agent
108	
109	No agent tool shows this meter or reads it. An agent reads a mix's loudness from an export's report, and `normalize_clip` reports a clip's measured loudness as it sets the volume. See [Tools: rendering and export](/mcp/tools-render-and-export/) and [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/#normalize_clip).
110

114	- [Normalize](/audio/normalize/)

116	- [Track compressor and limiter](/audio/track-dynamics/)

1	---
2	title: "Synchronize Audio"
3	description: Line up a camera and a separate recorder, or any clips of the same moment, by matching their sound.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	Synchronize Audio lines up two or more clips by their sound. The usual case is a camera clip and a separate audio recorder that captured the same moment. It finds where the sound matches, moves the clips into place and corrects any clock drift, all as one undo step.
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  menu="Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio"
13	  tools="sync_audio"
14	  needs="Nothing. The matching and the speech detection run on your Mac, with no key and no upload."
15	/>
16	
17	## Line up clips
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Put each clip on its own track. They don't need to be close to each other.
22	
23	2. If the recorder holds several similar stretches, trim it roughly around the camera's sound, so it [matches the right one](#matching-by-sound).
24	
25	3. [Select the clips](/timeline/selecting-clips/).
26	
27	4. Choose **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio**. It has no keyboard shortcut.
28	
29	5. Wait for the [Synchronizing Audio sheet](#the-synchronizing-audio-sheet) to finish.
30	
31	</Steps>
32	
33	One clip, the [anchor](#the-anchor), stays where it is. Every other clip slides along its own track until its sound plays at the same moment as the anchor's. The whole command is one undo step, named **Synchronize Audio**.
34	
35	If Frame Job is sure of the match, it's applied straight away. If it isn't, Frame Job [asks you first](/audio/weak-sync-matches/).
36	
37	It's all or nothing. If any clip can't be matched, nothing moves, and [the reasons are listed](#when-it-wont-run).
38	
39	If the clips are already in sync, nothing changes and Frame Job beeps. Choosing the command a second time on the same clips does this.
40	
41	## Which clips it takes
42	
43	**Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** is available when at least two selected clips can play sound and aren't [nests](/editing/nests/).
44	
45	Anything else in the selection is left out without a message: a nest, a still, a title, a file with no audio track, a clip with its audio switched off. To line up clips inside a nest, open it with <kbd>⌘↓</kbd> and select them there.
46	
47	## The anchor
48	
49	Frame Job picks the anchor this way:
50	
51	1. Among the selected clips that have a picture, the one that starts earliest. If none has a picture, all of them are considered.
52	2. If two start at the same time, the one on the rearmost track.
53	3. If they're still tied, the one created first.
54	
55	So a camera clip stays put and the recorder moves to it. The anchor is never moved or trimmed, and its speed doesn't change.
56	
57	## Matching by sound
58	
59	Each file's sound is analysed once, after it's imported, into a form that isn't thrown off by differences in gain, microphone or room. Frame Job compares the files, not the clips, so a clip's volume and effects make no difference.
60	
61	- **Speech comes first.** When both clips hold at least 2 seconds of speech, as judged by speech detection on your Mac, only the speech is compared. Otherwise all the sound is.
62	- **The trimmed parts come first.** Frame Job looks within the parts each clip is trimmed to, when both are at least 2 seconds long. It searches the whole files only if that finds no usable match and at least one clip is trimmed.
63	
64	:::tip
65	A recording with two similar stretches can match the wrong one. Trimming the recorder roughly around the camera's sound tells Frame Job which one you mean.
66	:::
67	
68	## The waveform check
69	
70	Sounding alike isn't enough, because two takes of the same words can look like a match. So a match is used only if the two waveforms also line up there, as a clear peak within 48 ms. Frame Job checks up to 30 seconds of the overlap, where the sound agrees most, in the speech band of 300 to 3,400 Hz.
71	
72	The same check fine-tunes the offset to less than a frame.
73	
74	## Moves land on whole frames
75	
76	Clips move by a whole number of frames at the project's frame rate, so up to half a frame of constant offset can remain. At 30 fps that's about 17 ms.
77	
78	## The head trim
79	
80	If a clip would have to start before 0:00 to line up, it loses that much from its start instead, and starts at 0:00 in sync. Frame Job trims only what it has to. It won't do this if less than a frame of the clip would be left.
81	
82	## Drift correction
83	
84	Two devices' clocks never run at quite the same rate, so a recorder slowly falls out of sync over a long take. When the clips overlap for at least 60 seconds, Frame Job measures that drift in 20-second windows along the overlap and corrects it by playing the moved clip at a slightly different speed, at most 0.2 % from ×1.
85	
86	The correction is part of the same undo step. There's no drift figure to read. What changes is the clip's speed, and **Keep pitch** is turned off. The [Speed section](/speed/speed-section/) shows the rate to two decimal places, so a correction such as ×1.0004 still reads 1.00× there. The clip gets very slightly longer or shorter to match.
87	
88	Drift is left alone when:
89	
90	- it's under 5 ms across the overlap
91	- it's too small to tell from no drift, meaning under three times its own uncertainty
92	- correcting it would take more than 0.2 % from ×1
93	- too little of the overlap matches to measure it
94	
95	:::note
96	The correction plays the sound slightly faster or slower, as tape would, so the pitch moves very slightly with the speed. Like any clip with Keep pitch off at a speed other than ×1, the clip's sound is [rendered in the background](/speed/keep-pitch/#tape-pitch-is-rendered-in-the-background). It's briefly silent in the preview after the correction, and again after each trim, split or speed change. An export waits for it.
97	:::
98	
99	## The Synchronizing Audio sheet
100	
101	Matching runs in the background behind a **Synchronizing Audio** sheet, with a progress bar and the line "Matching the sound of N clips…". Nothing moves until a match is found.
102	
103	**Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the sheet and leaves everything as it was.
104	
105	If the project changes while the matching runs, for example because an agent edits it or moves in or out of a nest, nothing is applied. Frame Job beeps and the inspector says to choose Synchronize Audio again.
106	
107	## When it won't run
108	
109	Frame Job beeps and lists every reason in [the strip at the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip), naming each clip by its number. The strip shows three lines, so hover over it to read a long one.
110	
111	It checks each clip first, and won't start matching until they all pass. A clip can't be lined up when it:
112	
113	- plays no sound in the timeline
114	- is still being analysed. Its sound or speech analysis hasn't finished, so try again in a moment.
115	- comes from a file with under 2 seconds of sound
116	- plays more than 0.2 % away from ×1. Set it back to ×1 first.
117	- plays at a different rate from the ×1 its speed shows, because its source is stretched
118	- plays [reversed](/speed/reverse/)
119	- [ramps its speed](/speed/speed-ramps/), because a speed action changes its rate over its length
120	
121	The rest come up during the matching:
122	
123	- Two of the clips are on one track. Each needs its own.
124	- A clip has no sound to line up by, because its analysis found no sound at all.
125	- Nothing matches. See [When nothing matches](/audio/weak-sync-matches/#when-nothing-matches).
126	- A clip matches the anchor's sound but the waveforms don't line up there, for example two takes of the same words. They aren't one recording.
127	- A clip matches the anchor's sound but the two share under 2 seconds of waveform there, too little to confirm it's one recording.
128	- A clip would lose so much of its head that less than a frame is left.
129	- A clip would never play at the same time as the anchor once lined up. Extend its trim, or the anchor's.
130	- A clip would overlap another clip on its own track after the move. Move that clip out of the way, or put this one on a free track.
131	
132	## With an agent
133	
134	`sync_audio` does the same thing. An agent can name the anchor, and it's told by name when it passes a nest or a clip that plays no sound, where the menu leaves those out. Its answer also gives each clip's offset, confidence, trim and drift, and clips already in sync are reported as such. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/#sync_audio).
135

1	---
2	title: "Confident and weak matches"
3	description: How Synchronize Audio grades a match, what the Weak match sheet asks you, and what to do when nothing matches.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	[Synchronize Audio](/audio/synchronize-audio/) grades every match it finds. A confident match is applied straight away, a weak one is asked about first, and anything less moves nothing.
10	
11	<AtAGlance menu="Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio" tools="sync_audio" />
12	
13	Each possible offset, meaning how far a clip could move to line up, gets a **confidence**: a score for how far it stands out from every other offset Frame Job tried. A high score means one offset is clearly right. Frame Job keeps up to four candidates, each about a second or more from the others.
14	
15	Either grade must also pass [the waveform check](/audio/synchronize-audio/#the-waveform-check). A match that fails it isn't used, however high its confidence, which keeps two takes of the same words apart.
16	
17	## Confident matches
18	
19	A match is confident when its best candidate has a confidence of at least 10, and is at least 1.5 above the next candidate. A confident match is applied straight away.
20	
21	## The Weak match sheet
22	
23	A match is weak when no candidate is confident, but the best one within about 3 seconds of where the clip already sits has a confidence of at least 4. A weak match might be unrelated sound, so it's never applied without asking. A **Weak match** sheet appears:
24	
25	> Weak match: move “record.aifc” 0.80 s earlier (trimming 0.80 s off its head)?
26	
27	A clip that doesn't need to move, only to have its drift corrected, is asked about this way:
28	
29	> Weak match: play “record.aifc” at ×1.0004, correcting its drift?
30	
31	When several clips are weak, one sheet lists them all, separated by semicolons.
32	
33	Under the question, the sheet gives the anchor's name, each match's confidence and the rule it fell short of.
34	
35	| Choose | What happens |
36	| --- | --- |
37	| **Apply** (the default) | Makes all the changes as one undo step, including those for any clips that matched confidently. |
38	| **Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> | Leaves everything as it is, including clips that matched confidently. |
39	
40	If you aren't sure, choose **Apply** and play the result. <kbd>⌘Z</kbd> takes all of it back in one step.
41	
42	If the project changed while the sheet was up, or an agent moved in or out of a nest, **Apply** moves nothing. Frame Job beeps and the inspector says to choose Synchronize Audio again.
43	
44	A weak match that wouldn't change anything isn't asked about.
45	
46	A weak match in the trimmed parts ends the search, and the whole files are searched only when the trimmed parts give neither a confident nor a weak match. So if you cancel a weak match, change the trims before trying again.
47	
48	## When nothing matches
49	
50	If no candidate is confident or weak, nothing moves. [The strip at the foot of the inspector](/getting-started/refused-edits/#the-refusal-strip) names the offsets Frame Job did find and their confidences, for example:
51	
52	> Refused: no matching sound found between clip 1 and clip 2: in the played windows, moving clip 2 by +0.77 s (confidence 4.31) or −12.40 s (3.90). A match applies on its own at…
53	
54	"The played windows" are the parts each clip is trimmed to, and "the whole files" are listed too when those were searched. A plus sign means later and a minus sign means earlier. Hover over the strip to read the whole message.
55	
56	To try again:
57	
58	<Steps>
59	
60	1. Pick the offset that looks right. You might know roughly where the clip belongs, or one figure may be well ahead of the others.
61	
62	2. Move the clip by about that much, so it sits within 3 seconds of the match.
63	
64	3. Choose **Clip ▸ Synchronize Audio** again. A candidate near the clip with a confidence of at least 4 now comes up as a weak match, as long as it passes the waveform check.
65	
66	</Steps>
67	
68	If the message ends "too little room to compare their sound", Frame Job found no candidates at all. Check that both clips have enough sound to compare, and try longer trims.
69	
70	## With an agent
71	
72	An agent gets no sheet. A weak match moves nothing and the agent is told the move it would make, so it should ask you. It applies the match by calling `sync_audio` again with `accept_weak: true`, and only once you've agreed to that move. See [Tools: audio](/mcp/tools-audio/#apply-a-weak-match).
73

1	---
2	title: Detach and Attach Audio
3	description: Split a clip's sound onto a linked clip of its own, keep the two in step, and merge them back into one clip.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Detach Audio splits a clip's sound onto its own clip, so you can trim, move or process the sound apart from the picture. Attach Audio merges the two back into one clip.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Clip ▸ Detach Audio', 'Clip ▸ Attach Audio']}
12	  keys={['⌥⌘D', '⇧⌥⌘D']}
13	  where="Clip tab ▸ Sound ▸ Mix"
14	  tools={['detach_audio', 'attach_audio', 'set_enabled']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Detach audio
18	
19	Select one or more clips and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>. **Clip ▸ Detach Audio** and the **Detach Audio** button in the [Mix section](/audio/pan-and-mono/) of the Sound sub-tab do the same. The menu item is greyed out until something is selected.
20	
21	Each selected clip splits in two, as one undo step named "Detach Audio":
22	
23	- The original clip keeps its picture, and its audio is switched off.
24	- A new clip appears on the track directly below. It plays only sound, from the same file, with the same in point, length and speed, and it keeps the original's audio settings and actions.
25	
26	If the clip is already on the bottom track, Frame Job adds a new track underneath for the sound. Otherwise the sound always goes on the next track down, so make room there first, or drag the sound to another track afterwards.
27	
28	The two clips are now a **linked pair**. Trim the sound on its own to make a [J-cut or L-cut](/audio/j-and-l-cuts/).
29	
30	### When Detach Audio won't work
31	
32	Frame Job beeps, changes nothing and shows the reason at the foot of the inspector:
33	
34	| The reason says | What it means |
35	| --- | --- |
36	| "…media 2 has no audio track" | The clip's file has no sound. |
37	| "…its audio is switched off" | The clip has already been detached, or its sound is otherwise off. |
38	| "…it is not a media clip" | The clip is text, a shape, a graphic, a picture, a freeze frame, a nest or an adjustment clip. |
39	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap by…, more than half of the shorter clip…" | The track below already has a clip where the sound would land. |
40	| "clip 4 would overlap more than one neighbour on one side…" | The sound would reach more than one clip on the track below. |
41	| "clips 4 and 7 would overlap, and clip 7 is an adjustment clip…" | The track below has an adjustment clip where the sound would land. |
42	
43	Any other overlap with one clip on the track below, up to half the shorter clip, is allowed and becomes a cross dissolve between the two.
44	
45	With several clips selected, the ones that can be detached are, and the rest are skipped. You only see a reason when none of them could be.
46	
47	## See which clips are linked
48	
49	Each half of a linked pair shows a link symbol after its kind symbol, in the clip's name strip. Select one and the other gets a dashed ring in your Mac's accent colour, because edits to one move both. See [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/#linked-clips).
50	
51	### A clip with its audio off
52	
53	A clip whose audio is off shows no waveform and no fade handles. A clip with its picture and its sound both off is drawn dimmed. The picture half of a linked pair has no Sound sub-tab, so select the sound half to change anything about the sound. See [Turn a clip's picture or sound off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/).
54	
55	## What stays in sync
56	
57	A linked picture and sound stay in step in time through your edits.
58	
59	| Edit | What happens to the pair |
60	| --- | --- |
61	| Move | Moving either clip moves both by the same amount. Only the clip you drag changes track, so you can drag the sound to another track and its picture stays where it is. When a move would take either clip past the start of the timeline, both stop together. |
62	| [Split](/editing/splitting/) | A split through both pairs the two halves on each side of the cut. When the cut only crosses one of the clips, the other stays linked to the piece it shares more time with, and the other piece loses its link. |
63	| [Duplicate](/editing/duplicate-clips/), [Nest](/editing/nests/) and [Ripple Delete](/editing/delete-clips/) | Take both clips. |
64	| [Copy and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/) | A selected picture brings its sound, so the pair pastes as a pair. A selected sound is copied on its own, and the pasted copy isn't linked to anything. |
65	| Ripple edits, [Close Gap and Insert Time](/editing/close-gaps/) | Move the other half too. |
66	| [Trim and roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone) | On the picture, the edit carries to the sound when their edges line up. On the sound, it moves the sound alone. |
67	| [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) | Slips both, as far as the one with less room allows. |
68	| Delete | Deleting the picture deletes its sound too. See [Remove a clip's sound](#remove-a-clips-sound). |
69	| [Speed](/speed/change-speed/) and [Reverse](/speed/reverse/) | Frame Job won't do these on a linked clip. See [Actions and speed](#actions-and-speed). |
70	
71	A ripple edit that would push a sound starting before its picture past the start of the timeline doesn't happen at all. The reason at the foot of the inspector says the sound "would start before 0".
72	
73	Locks win over links. A partner on a [locked track](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#lock-track) isn't moved, split, trimmed, slipped, duplicated, nested or deleted with its clip. **Copy** is the exception: a selected picture brings its sound even from a locked track.
74	
75	## Remove a clip's sound
76	
77	To drop a clip's sound for good, detach it, select the sound half and press <kbd>⌫</kbd>. The picture stays, silent, and its link is gone.
78	
79	Undo brings the sound back. Once the sound clip is gone, no control in the app turns the picture's own audio back on.
80	
81	## Attach audio
82	
83	Select either half of a pair and press <kbd>⇧⌥⌘D</kbd>, or choose **Clip ▸ Attach Audio**. The **Attach Audio** button in the Mix section does the same, but it's only there with the sound half selected, because the picture half has no Sound sub-tab.
84	
85	The picture's audio comes back on with the sound clip's audio settings, and the sound clip is removed. Its track stays, empty if nothing else is on it. With several pairs selected, each one merges, as one undo step named "Attach Audio".
86	
87	**Clip ▸ Attach Audio** is greyed out until the selection holds a linked clip. The button stays live, and beeps if the selection holds none.
88	
89	### When Attach Audio won't work
90	
91	The two halves have to match, because they're becoming one clip. They need the same start, length, in point and speed, and the same actions at the same times with the same curves. Otherwise the reason at the foot of the inspector says "clip 4's picture and clip 5's sound do not cover the same time; trim them to match before Attach Audio". This is what a J-cut or an L-cut does on purpose. Trim the two to the same start and end first, and remove or match any action you added to only one half.
92	
93	## Actions and speed
94	
95	The new sound clip gets a copy of every action, so volume actions keep working. An action that only changes the picture does nothing on the sound clip. See [How edits move actions](/motion/how-edits-move-actions/#detach-audio).
96	
97	A clip with a [speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/) keeps it: the sound clip's copy of the Speed actions gives it the same ramp, so the two stay in step.
98	
99	Frame Job won't change the speed or direction of either half while they're linked, because the two would have to be re-timed identically. That covers Speed, Reverse, rate stretch, [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/), and adding, moving, changing or removing a Speed action. The reason at the foot of the inspector says "clip 4 is linked to clip 5: Attach Audio before changing its speed or direction". During a drag, such as a rate stretch, nothing moves and no reason appears. Attach, make the change, then detach again.
100	
101	Attaching keeps the sound's work. The picture takes the sound clip's audio settings, and each of its actions takes the audio values of the sound clip's action at the same place.
102	
103	## With an agent
104	
105	[`detach_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#detach_audio) and [`attach_audio`](/mcp/tools-audio/#attach_audio) do what the **Clip** menu does, for the one clip you name in `clip`. For `attach_audio`, either half will do.
106	
107	`set_enabled` turns a clip's picture or sound on or off directly, which no control in the app does. After a detached sound has been deleted, it's the way to switch the picture's own audio back on. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#set_enabled).
108	
109	## Related

112	- [Pan and Mix to mono](/audio/pan-and-mono/)
113	- [Turn a clip's picture or sound off](/editing/enable-picture-and-sound/)
114	- [Reading a clip on the timeline](/timeline/reading-a-clip/)
115	- [Edit a ramped clip](/speed/edit-a-ramped-clip/)

1	---
2	title: J-cuts and L-cuts
3	description: Let a shot's sound start before its picture, or run on under the next shot, by trimming the sound half of a linked pair.
4	---
5	
6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
8	
9	A J-cut brings in the next shot's sound before its picture. An L-cut lets a shot's sound run on under the next shot. Both soften a cut, and in Frame Job both come from trimming the sound half of a [detached clip](/audio/detach-and-attach/).
10	
11	<AtAGlance
12	  keys={['W', 'E']}
13	  where={["Timeline: drag a detached sound clip's edge", 'Timeline: ⌥⇧-drag an edge to roll']}
14	  tools={['trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}
15	/>
16	
17	## Make a J-cut
18	
19	<Steps>
20	
21	1. Select the later shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd> to [detach its audio](/audio/detach-and-attach/#detach-audio).
22	
23	2. If the shot before it is detached too, drag this sound to a track of its own. See [Keep the sound off its neighbour](#keep-the-sound-off-its-neighbour).
24	
25	3. Drag the sound clip's start edge to the left.
26	
27	</Steps>
28	
29	The sound now begins before its picture. The picture stays where it is.
30	
31	## Make an L-cut
32	
33	<Steps>
34	
35	1. Select the earlier shot and press <kbd>⌥⌘D</kbd>.
36	
37	2. If the next shot's sound is on the track the sound went to, drag this sound to a track of its own.
38	
39	3. Drag the sound clip's end edge to the right.
40	
41	</Steps>
42	
43	The sound now runs on after its picture has ended.
44	
45	## Keep the sound off its neighbour
46	
47	When two neighbouring shots are both detached, their sounds sit side by side on one track. Lengthening one into the other overlaps them, and an overlap on a track is a [cross dissolve](/audio/crossfades/), not a split edit. On a track of its own, the sound overlaps nothing.
48	
49	## How far the sound can go
50	
51	A trim can only reveal what's in the file. The sound stops at the first or last frame of its media, and at the start of the timeline. Choose a shot with spare sound before its in point for a J-cut, or after its out point for an L-cut.
52	
53	The sound has to keep at least one frame. If it runs into another clip on its track, Frame Job allows an overlap of up to half the shorter clip and won't go further.
54	
55	## Trim and roll a sound clip alone
56	
57	The half you grab decides what moves. An edit on the sound moves only the sound. An edit on the picture also moves the sound when their edges line up. A lead you've already made isn't lined up, so trimming that picture's start leaves the sound alone.
58	
59	Dragging is what lengthens a sound. <kbd>W</kbd> and <kbd>E</kbd> [trim to the playhead](/editing/trimming/#trim-to-the-playhead), so they only shorten it, and they do it to the sound alone. To roll the cut between two sound clips on one track, hold <kbd>⌥⇧</kbd> and drag the edge between them. A sound on a track of its own has no cut to roll.
60	
61	See [Move a sound clip's edge alone](/editing/slip-and-roll/#move-a-sound-clips-edge-alone).
62	
63	## Good to know
64	
65	- Moving either half keeps the lead. When a drag would take the sound past the start of the timeline, both clips stop together.
66	- A ripple edit that would push a leading sound past the start of the timeline doesn't happen.
67	- Frame Job won't [attach](/audio/detach-and-attach/#attach-audio) a pair that no longer covers the same time. Trim the two to the same start and end first.
68	- [Slip](/editing/slip-and-roll/#slip-a-clip) takes both halves, unless the other half is on a locked track.
69	
70	## With an agent
71	
72	In the app, a trim on a sound moves it alone. An agent has to ask for that: pass `alone: true` to `trim_start`, `trim_end` or `roll` on the sound. Without it, a trim on a sound whose edge lines up with its picture moves both. See [Tools: moving and trimming](/mcp/tools-move-and-trim/#trim_start).
73

1	---
2	title: Mute and solo tracks
3	description: Silence a track, or hear only the tracks you pick, and see what that does to the picture, nests and an export.
4	---
5	
6	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
7	
8	Mute silences one track. Solo silences every other track, so you can hear one part of the mix by itself. Neither touches the picture.
9	
10	<AtAGlance
11	  menu={['Track ▸ Mute Audio', 'Track ▸ Solo']}
12	  where={['The speaker and headphones switches in the track header', "The track's right-click menu"]}
13	  tools="set_track"
14	/>
15	
16	## Mute a track
17	
18	Click the speaker switch in the track's header. Every clip on the track goes silent, and the picture is unaffected. Click it again to bring the sound back.
19	
20	**Mute Audio** in the track's right-click menu does the same for the track you clicked. **Track ▸ Mute Audio** acts on the [current track](/timeline/tracks/#the-current-track): the track of the first selected clip, or the front track when nothing is selected.
21	
22	To silence one clip and not its whole track, use its own [**Mute**](/audio/volume/#mute-a-clip).
23	
24	## Solo a track
25	
26	Click the headphones switch in the track's header, or choose **Solo** in the track's right-click menu or the **Track** menu. The tracks beside it go silent: the other timeline tracks or, inside a nest, that nest's other tracks.
27	
28	You can solo several tracks. All the soloed tracks play, and the rest are silenced.
29	
30	**Solo** shows a checkmark in the **Track** menu while it's on. Neither **Solo** nor **Mute Audio** has a keyboard shortcut. Each click is one undo step, named "Mute Track" or "Solo Track".
31	
32	## How mute and solo combine
33	
34	- **Mute always wins.** A track that's both muted and soloed stays silent.
35	- **Solo doesn't look at what's on the track.** A soloed track with nothing on it still silences the rest, as a mixer's solo button does.
36	- **Pictures stay.** A silenced track still draws. To take a picture out, use [Hide Video](/timeline/hide-and-lock-tracks/#hide-video), which leaves the sound playing.
37	
38	## See what a solo silences
39	
40	Under a solo, the waveforms on silenced tracks draw faded, as they do on a muted track. Their speaker switches stay unlit, because a speaker shows that track's own setting and not what a solo is doing to it. So the waveform tells you what you'll hear, and the switch tells you what you've set.
41	
42	## Mute and solo in nests
43	
44	A solo only reaches the tracks beside it:
45	
46	- A solo on a timeline track silences the other timeline tracks, and a nest playing on one of them goes silent with it.
47	- A solo on a track inside a [nest](/editing/nests/) affects only that nest's other tracks.
48	
49	Muting the track a nest clip sits on silences everything inside the nest. A new nest's tracks copy the mute and solo of the tracks they came from, so a muted track's clips stay silent once they're nested. Un-nesting doesn't keep what's set on the nest's tracks.
50	
51	## In an export
52	
53	Mute and solo are part of the project, so the export hears what you hear. A silenced track isn't in the exported mix, and it writes no [stem](/export/stems/). If every track is silenced, Frame Job won't write stems.
54	
55	:::caution
56	A solo left on silences the rest of the export. Check the header switches before you export.
57	:::
58	
59	## Good to know
60	
61	- The switches are plain toggles. <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking one does what a click does, and <kbd>⌥</kbd>-clicking the header away from its switches [selects the track's clips](/timeline/tracks/#the-track-header).
62	- A [scrub](/audio/scrub-audio/) plays the same mix, so mute and solo silence it too.
63	- The header's other switches are on [The track header](/timeline/tracks/#the-track-header).
64	
65	## With an agent
66	
67	`set_track` sets the same switches. Name the `track` and pass `muted` or `solo` as true or false. It's a direct setting, not a toggle, so asking for what's already set changes nothing. See [Tools: tracks, markers and canvas](/mcp/tools-tracks-and-markers/#set_track).
68
